38.content:
**Minecraft 1.21.1.** Four files now: 26.3 and 1.21.1, each for Fabric and NeoForge, from one codebase — every future
update reaches both versions together. On 1.21.1 you need Java 21, Fabric Loader 0.20.1 with Fabric API 0.116.17 or
NeoForge 21.1.265, GeckoLib 4.9.3 and TerraBlender 4.1.0.8.

39.content:
**Blocks from 26.x on 1.21.1.** Where  builds on things 1.21.1 does not have, the 1.21.1 files bring their own that
behave as in 26.3: pale oak and poplar wood (full sets and saplings; poplar leaves come yellow, orange or red), short and
tall dry grass, pale moss with its carpet and hanging moss, the copper nugget, copper tools, copper armor and copper horse
armor. They grow and generate where the mod puts them on 26.3 and fit the same recipes.

40.content:
**Dappled Forest and Pale Garden on 1.21.1.** All of this can now be found in survival just as on 26.3: poplars in three
colors grow in the Dappled Forest, pale oak with pale and hanging moss in the Pale Garden (both biomes generate where they do
on 26.3 — on cool dry plains and on humid dark forest plateaus), dry grass in deserts and badlands, copper horse armor lies
in the same chests of dungeons, temples, fortresses, End cities and weaponsmiths, and the wandering trader sells pale oak
and poplar saplings and logs, pale and hanging moss and dry grass, as on 26.3.

41.content:
**Mechanics — a branch for Create** (1.21.1, NeoForge, Create 6.0.10). The Stream Wheel turns shafts with your chunk's
flux (twice as fast where a Gauge Stone speeds the flux); the Windlass gives shaft power to the Stamp Mill, the Molder, the
Sluice Box and the Pump; the Crucible Stirrer sinks solids even over a gentle heat; the Drip Tap fills vials on belts and
depots, and the Decanting Trough pours them back into vessels, the Crucible and the Gyre. The Mechanical Arm tends
Confluence plinths, the Crucible and workshop devices; an Ember Shard superheats a blaze burner; fans blowing through Orbs
wear, mend, dry, set and rinse blocks; Create's machines crush, press and mix the mod's materials. Diviner's Spectacles
work as engineer's goggles, display boards show chunk flux and held currents, six Ponder scenes and a Codex tab with 13
entries explain it all.

218.content:
**Aptitudes** grow the fluxionist themself. Seven aptitudes stand on a seal like currents on the Wheel, and each pulls on its own
craft of : not "the strongest", but "a little easier where you have invested". Steps are bought with **Insights** — the fruits
of the path you have walked. The aptitude sheet is the Aptitudes tab in the Codex, under the Wheel ribbon.

227.content:
**Intellect** grows first readings only: repeats, Desk techniques and other note sources stay as they are. The fraction builds up
by chapter and arrives as a whole note later — nothing is lost to rounding.

228.content:
**Might** works on the mod's things: fluxsteel, Spring Tools, wootz, freshet and still gear, all of 's weapons. A weapon
ability's strike grows by the same share.

229.content:
**Finesse** and **Will** are thrift under a shared limit: crafting and casting never get cheaper than half price, however many
aptitudes and gear pieces add up.

230.content:
**Patience** reduces losses rather than multiplying output: extra currents from nothing would turn the "dissolve — brew" loop
into profit.

231.content:
**Will** does not lift Dissonance — that is the price of knowledge; it only lets a vision through less often at a check. The
Metronome already hears this chance.

232.content:
**Poise** is the starter's gift to a Confluence, the same as gear's, and under the same limit: with a full set of gear gifts it
adds almost nothing. It is a choice of "wear or grow".

233.content: Insights are neither saved nor stored: your knowledge counts them, so they cannot be ground out, lost or earned twice.

234.content: **The path walked**: the first Insight comes with your 8th studied entry, then one every 20.

235.content: **The first victory over each master and lair guardian** — an Insight for everyone who fought.

236.content: Entries written in from someone else's Fair Copy give no Insights: the Fair Copy passes on knowledge, not the path walked.

237.content:
The aptitude sheet counts what the whole path gives: right now the whole Codex is 19 Insights and victories up to 10 more,
against 35 ranks across all aptitudes. Whoever has not walked it all chooses where to invest; "everything at once" never happens,
not even at the end.

238.content:
When an Insight arrives — a mod line above the hotbar, a soft chime and sparks over your head; the Aptitudes ribbon in the Codex
glows and carries "+N".

239.content:
Open the Aptitudes tab. The seal is seven medallions: Intellect on top, Will at the bottom, the Springs on the sides in the Wheel's
order, Poise in the middle. The ring around a medallion is its five rank segments. A medallion you can develop breathes amber, and a
brass "+" button surfaces by it. Press it, or pick the aptitude and press Develop on its page — a rank costs one Insight. An
aptitude's page tells what it gives now, what the next rank will give and where it works.

240.content:
What you have invested can be taken back at a : the Codex opened from the Desk window shows a Rewrite
button on the sheet's overview. All ranks become free Insights again for **experience levels** — a level per invested Insight, but
no fewer than five. Intellect's fraction stays: it is already earned.

241.content:
Some dishes and effects raise an aptitude for a while — for example, the Kitchen of Currents dishes with Farmer's Delight. Boosts
do not add up: the biggest one counts, and nothing goes above the fifth rank. They do not touch the aptitude sheet or Insights.

242.content:
No entry, board, structure or fight requires an aptitude rank. The economy of notes, the prices and the limits hold without them:
aptitudes make easier what you like to do, they do not unlock what is closed. Every player's aptitudes are their own and survive
death and relogging; the Fair Copy does not copy them.

259.content:
**Build a 3×3×3 cube**: copper at the eight corners, a magma block at the heart, a copper grate in the middle of the front
(the tap hole) and in the middle of the top (the throat), everything else . The diagram is in the
Codex; "Place ghost" sets it in the world.

260.content:
**Wake it** with a pinch of quickdust on any block: copper binds the masonry, flux veins show in the joints, the magma wakes as
the forge's heart. Break any block and the forge falls apart into what it was built from.

front of it, otherwise onto the ground. Every third ore drips : dissolve it in the Crucible and the
ore gives up its currents.

297.content: A workshop inside a dense skein: the Embroidery Hoop, entering and leaving, size by winding, nature and flux from the threads, carrying it on a Spindle.

306.content: Your workshop will not be lost

309.content:
Your own workshop wherever it suits you. A dense skein is opened with an Embroidery Hoop — inside it is a **Bower**, a small
world to build in. Its ground, sky and flux are the threads of the skein: a skein of Ember gives warm ground and Ember of the
place, a skein of Tide gives water and drizzle. Wind more — the Bower grows; carry the skein on a Spindle — the whole workshop
goes with it. The Codex entry is , in the Artifice chapter, after the Spindle.

310.content:
The  is two lumenash rings on a brass screw with a thread stretched between them. It is made
at the Flux Workbench: 32 flux, with Lattice and Gale of the place.

311.content:
**The threshold is density.** A skein opens once it holds **96 shares or more** (all threads together): a medium one three
quarters full, or a large one. A small skein (64 shares) never opens. How threads are wound and tied on — the entry
.

312.content:
**These do not open**: a greedy skein (it tears the hoop), a turbulent one (the threads would burst — bring in Lattice first),
a still one (it does not stretch). A murky skein opens — but its Bower is murky too.

313.content:
**The rite**: hold the hoop on the skein for **3 seconds**. The threads stretch onto the ring and the skein goes still; look
away and the rite breaks off, the skein unharmed. When it is done, the hoop goes into the skein and becomes its ring: that is
the key of the Bower. Whoever opened it is the **owner**.

314.content:
A skein with a Bower shows from afar: the hoop's ring around its equator, and in it a window with slow ribbons of thread. A
sleeping Bower's window is dark. The Loupe writes the Bower's line: whether it is open, its size and owner — and for a sleeping
one, how many shares it lacks.

315.content:
**To enter**, hold the open skein **with an empty hand for 2 seconds** — the threads wrap around you, the edges of your view
close in ribbons of the threads' colors, and the "Into the Skein" screen draws you in. Let go early and the count starts over.

316.content:
**To leave**, find the **Loose End** hanging from the sky of the Bower. Hold it for **1.5 seconds** — the "Out of the Skein"
screen brings you out where the skein hangs: to the nearest spot where you can stand, under it and around it.

317.content:
**A skein over water**: if there is nowhere to step nearby, you come out on the nearest shore within 32 blocks, a little more
readily on the side you entered from. Open sea all around — onto the surface right under the skein; swim from there.

318.content: The owner moves the Loose End with the hoop on a face of the ground inside the Bower.

319.content: Leave the game inside and you come back in the same spot. Dying inside means an ordinary respawn; the items stay in the Bower.

320.content: There is no night inside a skein: you cannot sleep or set your spawn here.

321.content:
The owner invites guests: **the hoop on a player** — "Became a guest" or "No longer a guest". A guest enters all of the owner's
Bowers **while the owner is inside**, builds and breaks like the owner, and may wind and open a skein with a Bower. Only the
owner can unravel a Bower or call it back by the rite. A stranger without an invitation hears "Someone else's Bower: the owner has not
invited you" and cannot carry it off on a Spindle.

322.content: The side of the Bower follows **the greatest winding** since it was opened:

328.content:
A medium skein grows to 24 × 24, a large one to 48 × 48 — and one merged into a large skein by a Swift too (the entry
). **A Bower grows but never shrinks**: draw the threads off and the side stays, what you built
stays. It grows while someone is inside: a new band of ground rises around the old one, the sky flares and a wave of threads
runs along the edge.

329.content:
The edge of the Bower is the **Winding**: a wall of wound thread around it, under the ground and above the sky. Nothing passes
through it — no player, water, lava or dragon; no pickaxe, blast or wither breaks it. Come within seven blocks and the threads
show as a mesh of slanting strands. You can build only inside the Winding.

330.content:
Every current of the skein is one of eleven kinds of nature. The **leading thread** (the fullest) gives the ground, the
**second** gives an admixture (about a quarter of the cells), and if the leading and second threads combine on the Wheel, the
admixture is their compound: Tide and Ember make Bloom — flowers. Ground is laid once, as a band is built: a band grown later
takes the nature of the threads at that time — the Bower changes ring by ring. The sky, light, fog and drizzle always follow
the threads.

342.content:
**The sky is the inside of the skein**: overhead, all around and under the ground lie the dense windings of the skein itself,
as if seen from inside a ball of yarn, in the colors of its threads. The leading thread gets more windings. The sky drifts
slowly: the skein turns, and beads of flux run along the strands. A steady skein winds evenly, a murky one sags, wanders and
darkens, a lucent one winds thinner, with a gleam. Time stands still in a Bower: it is always day; with Dark the sky and light
are dimmer, with Light brighter. There is no weather — only the drizzle and motes of its kind.

343.content:
**The riverbed of every chunk of the Bower comes from the threads**: 24 plus a third of all the shares of the skein
(96 shares give 56, 128 give 67, 256 give 109 — almost a river). Draw threads off and the riverbed drops; tie more on and it
rises. Beyond the Winding there is no riverbed: flux never leaves a Bower.

344.content:
**The currents of the place are the threads of the skein** holding **8 shares or more**: the Flux Workbench, the Crucible, the
, Current Seeds and the Loupe all see them. A skein of Ember makes Ember of the place in its Bower:
Ember recipes without shards.

345.content:
**Devices spend flux** as anywhere, and the chunk refills up to its riverbed. The threads themselves are not spent inside: only
outside — by siphons, flasks, the Conduit and rewinding.

346.content:
**Murk settles** as anywhere: a careless Bower grows murky, mire takes root and Snarls are born. Murk above a third of the
riverbed for five minutes straight turns the skein itself murky. The cure is the same as outside: a 
inside, Halo tied on the skein; a lucent skein cleans its Bower's murk by itself.

347.content: While nobody is inside, the Bower is not loaded: its flux and murk stand still.

348.content:
**Carry it on a Spindle**: everyone inside is gently set out where the skein hung. Unwind the 
somewhere else — the same Bower, everything in place, and the way in is there now. Rewinding costs an eighth of the threads,
as always.

349.content:
**Threads below the threshold** (96) — the Bower **sleeps**: the way in is closed, anyone inside leaves as usual. Tie threads
back on and it opens.

350.content:
**Neighbors**: a skein with a Bower shares threads with its neighbors like any other but never merges by itself — only the Swift
of the owner or a guest merges it, and it is always the one that draws the other in. Two skeins with Bowers never merge: a Bower
has one door.

351.content:
**The skein is destroyed** — by any means — and it furls into a  holding its threads (less an
eighth) and the key. Fire, lava and blasts do not take it, it never vanishes from the ground, and it does not stack. Unwind it
on a block face like a Spindle — and the Bower is back, everything as it was. Whoever was inside comes out where the skein hung.

352.content:
**Lost it entirely** (fell into the void, burned in a chest) — the owner calls the Bower back **by the rite**: the hoop with
Shift on a fresh dense skein without a Bower, of the same leading thread. The old skein, if it turns up, becomes a plain skein:
there are never two doors.

353.content:
**Only the owner can erase a Bower**: inside, the hoop with Shift on the Loose End opens the "Unravel the Bower?" window; the
button is held for 3 seconds. Everything inside is gone for good, the skein stays a skein without a Bower, and the hoop goes back
to the owner.

354.content:
Every Bower is a plot of its own, far from its neighbors. Sound and events from one Bower reach neither another one nor the
outside: a blast, thunder, a summoned wither or a dragon's death in yours is heard by you alone. Ender pearls, chorus fruit,
Through-Circles and mirrors never lead into someone else's Bower, and creatures — even a dragon — never get past the Winding.
You can always leave a Bower: by the Loose End, by a Nether portal or by dying.

367.content:
A current circle is an ink drawing on a field of slabs underfoot. Put currents into its three sockets and the circle does the
work itself: tills, reaps, heals, keeps monsters out, smelts, carries you to its pair. It pays with the flux of its own chunk
and leaves almost no murk. Codex entries — , , 
and four rite entries.

368.content:
Lay **bottom**  in a square at one height: **3 × 3** — a small circle, **5 × 5** — a great one.
The slabs are dry and not taken by another circle.

369.content:

The circle's arrow points where you face.

with an empty hand — the last socket back. Sneaking with the Ruling Pen — erase the circle (the slabs stay, the items go to you).

373.content: **Any slab broken** — the whole circle falls apart, socketed items drop at the middle. Pistons don't move circle slabs.

374.content: **A redstone signal** on any slab puts the circle to sleep — that is how you switch a rite off with a lever.

current. Won't brew without the  entry.

378.content: **Only glyphs wake rites.** A circle whose filled sockets are all glyphs works one block wider.

379.content:
Socket currents add up **along the Wheel**: if two currents make a third, the circle reads the sum too. The combination is exact —
an extra current throws the circle off ("The sockets add up to nothing").

380.content:

a half riverbeds — 4, in flood — 5. An all-glyph circle is one block wider, **a great one two more** (up to 8). Every deed takes
the flux of its chunk, but never below the riverbed floor: on drained land the circle waits.

409.content:
Bans on a place ("nothing explodes here", "no monsters spawn here") are not circles but totems: a circle
does work, a totem holds a law.

410.content: Two circles — an entrance and an exit: stand on one, crouch — and you are on the other.

411.content: Sockets — ,  and  glyphs: a lone Through-Circle.

412.content: Press one more Bind glyph against it — it remembers the circle (tooltip "Remembers the Through-Circle at x, y, z").

413.content: Put it into a second circle's socket together with Shift and Drift — a pair. The far circle may be asleep: the pair is a world record.

414.content:
**Step**: stand inside the rim and crouch; after a second and a half (30 ticks) you are in the middle of the far circle, facing
along its arrow. Step off — canceled. Cooldown — 5 s. Your own pets standing on the circle come along — up to two. The circle
carries no items and no other creatures — items go through Through-Mirrors.

415.content: **Cost** — flux of the departure chunk: 4 + 1 per 100 blocks, up to 16; between worlds — 24. No murk, no Dissonance.

416.content:
**Worlds**: a small circle leads within its own world; between the Overworld, the Nether and the End — only **great circles on
both sides**. The circle does not lead into the mod's worlds.

417.content: **Owner** — whoever socketed the last glyph. Sneaking, press with any glyph to open the circle to guests or close it.

418.content: The far land is not kept loaded: it arrives for the moment of the step and leaves on its own.

The chapters of compatibility branches (Energistics, Kitchen of Currents, Spirits) open when the mod they need is installed. Without
it the chapter's tab is dim, with a lock and a red Needs mod line, and its entries **cost nothing**: they cannot be studied and
their puzzles cannot be opened — so you never spend resources on a branch you cannot reach anyway.

444.content:
Entries lie on a canvas and are joined by streams: what you study flows into what follows from it. Drag the page with the mouse to
walk along the riverbed. A previous entry may stand in another chapter — then Study first names it.

445.content:
| State   | What it means             |
| ------- | ------------------------- |
| Studied | the entry is open in full |

446.content:
| State          | What it means                                     |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Ready to study | the previous ones are studied and you know enough |

447.content:
| State                | What it means                                              |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Needs more knowledge | the previous ones are studied, but you know too little yet |

448.content:
| State  | What it means                                                    |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sealed | the previous ones are not studied — or a mod it needs is missing |

449.content:
Under an unstudied entry's title is its **lure**: what to do to open it. The Codex opens itself on an entry you can study, and
once you know enough for a new one, a line above the hotbar says Ready to study.

450.content: An entry asks for one or more kinds of knowledge:

451.content:
**notes** of chapters — first readings with the Loupe bring them (The Loupe); studying **spends**
them;

452.content: **readings** — read a certain thing, block, creature or place with the Loupe, or witness an event (any one from the list will do);

453.content: **revealed currents** — read a thing that has the current.

454.content:
When you know enough, press **Study**: the notes soak into the text, streams in the chapter's color gather to the book, the entry
opens, and the next ones surface behind it. Some entries also take a share of Dissonance — the price knowledge takes from
the mind (Dissonance and Visions).

455.content:
Many entries are studied not with the button but by solving a **riverbed puzzle** at a . A lectern
sprinkled with quickdust becomes a Reckoning Desk; lay the Codex on it (use the Desk with the Codex in hand) and use it — a window
opens with the puzzles you can open now: price, board size, state. Sneak with an empty hand to take the Codex back.

456.content:
The puzzle is yours, not the Desk's: two can work at one Desk, each with a board of their own, and an abandoned puzzle waits as it
was — at any Desk. Every fluxionist has the same boards, so solutions can be discussed.

457.content:
The board is a map of a riverbed. Along the edge are **springs** (each pours the current of its rune) and **outlets** (each waits
for its own). Channels are drawn with the : drag from a spring across neighboring cells.

458.content: **Downhill or level**: the number in a cell's corner is its height. A channel does not flow uphill.

459.content: **Stone** blocks a channel, and a channel that runs into a **pit** cannot climb out.

460.content:
**Merging by the Wheel**: two channels meeting in a cell merge — Gale and Tide give Drift, Ember and Gale give Spark. No more
than two channels meet in one cell.

461.content: **A basin**: the only place where opposite Springs merge — Tide and Ember give Bloom.

462.content:
**A Pole sign** pulls a current passing through it: Ember through a Lattice sign comes out as Gleam. To a current with no
combination with that Pole, the sign is stone. Channels do not merge on a sign.

463.content: An unrevealed current cannot be led: read a thing it flows in with the Loupe.

464.content:
| Mark | What it does                                                                 |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fork | the cell gets a second exit: the channel splits in two with the same current |

465.content:
| Mark     | What it does                                                                            |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Aqueduct | a channel passes across another without merging; only on plain ground, running straight |

466.content:
| Mark | What it does                                                   |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Lock | a channel may enter this cell from a neighbor one height lower |

467.content:
| Mark  | What it does                                                      |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Basin | a Crucible by the Desk: one plain cell becomes a basin — for free |

468.content:
Each mark costs **a note of the entry's chapter**. A segment of channel takes a division of ink; a full pen holds **96 divisions**,
and erased ink does not come back. A dry pen is refilled with an ink sac and any current shard.

469.content:
Your hand holds **techniques**: three, plus one for every three milestones studied, up to six; each is played once. The common
ones: **Hunch** (threads from the outlets to the springs), **Redo** (erases the last three segments and returns their ink),
**Ponder** (one more technique), **Leveling** (a 3 × 3 square settles to its average height), **Set Aside** (one outlet may stay
unfed, but the riverbed is no longer clean), **Trial** (a spring changes its current). Neighbors within four steps of the Desk
lend their own:

470.content:
| Neighbor    | What it gives                                         |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| a bookshelf | Reference (correct segments penciled in) and Transfer |

471.content:
| Neighbor            | What it gives                                                          |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| an enchanting table | Table Lore: 5 experience levels become 6 notes of the puzzle's chapter |

472.content:
| Neighbor | What it gives                     |
| -------- | --------------------------------- |
| a beacon | Beacon Light: two more techniques |

Chapters add techniques of their own: the Conduit — Aim, Keen Eye and the Flux Vow; Hour Marks — the Hour Check (the next
lock and aqueduct for free).

476.content: **Opening a puzzle** costs the entry's notes. The solved puzzle is the study itself.

477.content:
**A clean riverbed** — a solution no longer than the board's measure (the window shows the segment count) and without Set Aside:
a third of the price comes back as notes.

478.content: **Start Over** — the same board on a clean sheet and a new hand for half the price (the lesson has no such button).

479.content: Out of notes — Table Lore at the Desk.

480.content:
The  hands a friend everything your Codex knows, all at once: a friend who joins when you are already near
the Stillness need not start from quickdust. Take a blank fair copy and use it on the Desk holding your Codex: your studied entries
(boards solved), revealed currents and readings are copied in. Your friend takes it in hand and right-clicks — the knowledge becomes
theirs, and the fair copy is blank again.

481.content: Filling a fair copy costs half a pen of ink (48 divisions).

482.content: Notes are not copied; entries written in from someone else's fair copy are not passed on further and give no Insights.

483.content: Entries with Dissonance take half their Dissonance from the reader, no more than 10.

Under the chapter ribbons is the **Aptitudes** tab: growing the fluxionist with Insights that studied entries and first victories
bring (Aptitudes). In the game's advancements window (L),  has its own Fluxionist tab — 45
milestones of the path; the Codex is the path itself, the advancements only reflect it.

Energistics chapter.

499.content:
**** … **256k** — AE2 cells for currents, for the Drive and the ME Chest. A cell is a
 plus an AE2 storage component of the same size. Up to 18 kinds of currents per cell; an empty
one comes apart in your hand when you sneak.

500.content:
**** — for a network that holds the whole Wheel: 1024k, 63 kinds, more than six million shares and
not a drop of idle energy. It can't be taken apart.

501.content:
**Murk** isn't taken by ordinary cells. Only the **** holds it (4k, Murk alone): with it Murk piles up for
Murk Flasks, Druses and vats. No Sump cell — the network refuses Murk, and the workshop chooses: keep the cell or murk the land.

502.content:
Currents show in the AE2 terminal as runes next to items and fluids; the key-type filter is "Currents". **A vial on a current in the
terminal** fills it (a click — one share, Shift — as much as fits, up to 8); **a filled vial on the terminal** empties it. A vial
also sets the current in the slots of buses, processing patterns and the Interface.

|     | on any side of a vessel, Gyre or Alembic | the network sees its store, takes and puts like a vial |

Per step — 4 shares per operation; AE2 acceleration cards work as on its own buses. Empty slots — the Siphon Bus takes everything,
the Pouring Bus nothing.

The **** — a holder for siphons whose distillate is the whole network: a siphon above pours into the
network, a siphon at the side takes from it. The whole siphon workshop talks to the network through one block.

513.content:
The **** — the network's Wheel of Currents floats above its lens; the Loupe reads the count, a comparator
how many currents (up to 15).

514.content:

slot from the network.

515.content:
The **** — a network for automatons and hoppers: nine intake slots go into the network, nine stock slots

Accelerator run from it without a network.

Tower — Crucible recipes ordered from the terminal. The AE2 Level Emitter works with currents by itself.

518.content:
The mod has no energy of its own, and none for free: an ME network is powered by a Flux Mill at an
AE2 Energy Acceptor, and the land dries up as from any work. Distillate isn't burned for energy.

531.content:
Create for Minecraft 26.3 is not out yet, so the Mechanics branch exists **only for Minecraft 1.21.1 and only on NeoForge**
(the official Create 6.0.10). There is no Create for Fabric 1.21.1: the branch's items stand silent, their tooltip carries a red
"Needs mod: Create (NeoForge only)" line, and the Codex chapter "Mechanics" is locked. Minecraft 26.3 has no such branch at all —
it switches on when Create comes out for 26.x.

532.content:
With Create a fluxionist and a master of shafts work for each other: the flux of the land turns shafts, a shaft does the work
of muscles in the workshop, Create belts carry vials, and Create machines know the things of . What a shaft will not do:
make flux (every chunk has its own bed, and Create wheels turn forever) or pay for magic — flux crafting, the Confluence and a cast
still take the flux of the place. Distillate is not a fluid: it does not go through Create pipes or tanks; vials carry it. Entries —
the Codex chapter "Mechanics" (13 entries); in the game every item of the branch has a Ponder scene: hold W over it.

533.content:
The **** is a Create rotation source where there is neither water nor wind: flux rises in the flume and falls as a stream
onto the opaline paddles. 16 RPM and up to 256 stress units — by the chunk's free flux, in eighths. Under load the wheel drinks flux
(half a flux a second for a full load), idle — nothing; at the very floor of the bed it stirs up murk — dark flakes run in the
stream. **Where a Gauge Stone or your own Gauge Post speeds the flux of the chunk, the wheel turns twice as fast — 32 RPM — with the
same capacity.**

534.content:
The **** gives the turn of a shaft to the device it faces (the shaft at the back, from 16 RPM): a Stamp Mill pounds without
Cog, a Molder crafts without flux (from 64 RPM — twice as often), a Sluice Box washes twice as often, a Pump lifts distillate without
flux.

535.content: A pair for vials on a Create belt:

536.content:
The **** hangs under a vessel (or another distillate holder) and fills vials on a belt or depot one empty block below:
the shaft turns its screw, at 16 RPM a vial takes 6.4 s. It never pours Murk.

537.content:
The **** works the other way: it sits on a vessel, a Crucible or a Gyre; vials ride into it from a belt at its
back, drop in from above, or a mechanical arm lays them in; the shaft decants the vial part by part into the holder, and the empty
vial leaves at the front. The holder takes by its own rules (bed, brand, stopper): a full one is never forced — the vial waits in
the cradle. Murk and sealed vials pass by.

538.content:
The **** sits right on a Crucible, the shaft from above. From 32 RPM the paddle grinds what is hard: metals and stone
sink even over a gentle heat — a campfire will do (taking as much water as a strong one). The stirrer does not cancel a clash of
currents.

539.content:
A Create mechanical arm lays a thing on a Confluence plinth and lifts it off, drops things into a Crucible, lays vials into a
Decanting Trough, and works the devices whose slots go by faces (Stamp Mill, Sluice Box, Molder, Retort, Fish Trap, Flux Forge, Flux
Workbench, Brewing Tower): it puts into the input as a hopper from above and takes what is done as a hopper from below. It does not
begin a Confluence, flux crafting or a cast — it has no knowledge.

540.content:
**Millstone** — a shard of a primal current into 3 pinches of Grit; **crushing wheels** — antimony and opaline ores; **press** —
a speculum sheet; **heated mixer** — the blend straight into ingots; **sequenced assembly** — the Simple and Compound Drive without
flux; **item application** — a sheet on lumenash gives Speculum-Clad Lumenash.

541.content:
A **blaze burner** under a Crucible: kindled — a gentle heat, superheated — a strong one. An **Ember shard** superheats the burner
like a blaze cake, for 80 seconds. An **Ember Orb** heats a steam engine's boiler, and a fan through it smelts as through lava.

542.content:
**A draft through an Orb**: an encased fan blowing through an Orb processes things with its current — Fray ages copper and cracks
bricks, Lattice mends them back, Gale dries, Strata sets concrete, Tide rinses. One thing for one, nothing more.

543.content: A **fan at the tuyere** of a Flux Forge (from 32 RPM) counts as a Gale Fan.

712.content:
The Crucible dissolves things, the Workbench puts them together, and **Confluence** pours currents into the thing itself. It gives
what neither the Crucible nor a workbench can: weavings in tools and armor, exact enchantments, the power of trinkets and the strongest
things of fluxion. The Codex chapter is Confluence, its first entry  (after the
Conduit and Distillate).

plinth is the one that changes.

714.content:
**Side plinths** — up to sixteen, within eight blocks: one thing on each, to flow into the central one. Set them in an even ring —
two rings of eight, near and far: streams heaped on one side churn, and so do streams that cross from above.

715.content: **Four**  stand two blocks from the central plinth on each side: by them the Heart knows its altar.

716.content: Once it is built, throw a pinch of quickdust on the Heart: it wakes, and golden veins run from the columns and plinths to the center.

**Fold it with quickdust.** Sprinkle  on the heart or any block of a finished tower — it folds into one

794.content:
Empty hand through the niche (or on any part) — the window. On the left is the **mirror of place**: 128 blocks around the heart,
the grown part in the new place's color, a thin ring — the limit. On the right — the native place, the places you can grow (each
with the runes of its feed), the feed in the heart and the buttons **Grow**, **Rest**, **Restore**. While a growth owns something,
another target can't be chosen — restore first.

795.content:
**Feed** —  (change) and two currents of the new place. Vessels and Gyres within 6 blocks give them, and
a siphon from above through the crown. The heart holds up to 16 shares of each.

796.content: **Cost**: a share of each current per 8 biome cells, plus 0.25 flux of the heart's chunk per cell. Speed — at most 1.5 cells a second.

797.content:
The whole circle to the limit (about 2,420 cells) is about 27 minutes of well-fed work, about 300 shares of each feed current and
about 600 flux. You don't have to grow to the end: **Rest** stops the growth at any radius. A grove of radius 32 is about 25 shares
of each, radius 64 — about 100.

798.content: **Restore** — the same path back to the heart: the native place, its grass and trees; feed — one Shift and flux.

799.content:
A broken heart: its feed goes into the chunk as murk, the growth stops, **what has grown stays**. A new heart in the same spot
picks the growth up.

800.content: It grows only in the Overworld.

801.content:
The growth starts as an even circle at the heart, then its edge becomes uneven, lobed, with a band about 14 blocks wide where
cells of the old and the new place mix. The game blends grass and water colors itself — the transition is soft.

802.content:
Natural trees at the front go into flux (no drops), grass and flowers become the new place's plants, its trees and flowers rise,
and in an almost grown chunk its creatures are born.

803.content:

water and its bed, seas and oceans. Ground right next to a building changes like everywhere else. The biome itself is written on

835.content:
The  dissolves things into currents and brews new things out of them: fluxsteel for devices, wax for
vessels, opaline, quickdust, tonics, light without a candle, and glints. It is the fluxionist's first big workshop — the Codex
chapter Alchemy begins with it.

836.content:
The Crucible is not forged or crafted — it is woken. A pinch of  on a plain cauldron (empty or
filled): a whirl of the four Springs, a ring of Tide, and the cauldron turns to bronze, its feet become paws, opaline shows
along the rim. Waking needs no knowledge, but the Crucible's recipes are opened by Codex entries, starting with
.

837.content:
**Water by the bucket.** A full Crucible is one bucket — that is its whole measure. You can scoop the bucket back, but then
whatever is dissolved splashes out as murk into the land around; a broken Crucible spills it the same way.

838.content: **Heat comes from the block below.** Without heat the Crucible is just a bowl: what you throw in lies on the bottom.

839.content:
**Gentle heat** — a campfire, fire, magma, a lit furnace, an . It dissolves soft things: herbs,
flesh, coal, dust, wax.

840.content: **Strong heat** — lava or a lava cauldron. It dissolves everything that has currents.

841.content:
**Solid** things are those where ,  and  make up half
of the currents or more: metals, stone, glass, gems. In gentle heat they do not sink — they float up and fly over the rim.
That way iron is not lost in a Crucible over a campfire.

842.content: A thing without currents never sinks, whatever the heat.

843.content:
**Water boils away**: a bucket lasts 16 minutes of gentle heat and 8 of strong; every dissolved thing drinks more, and
brewing a recipe more still. Boiled dry, the distillate scorches and all of it goes to murk.

844.content:
Dissolved currents become **distillate** — a current in liquid form. It is tinted by the mix of its currents, and strands
of the fullest ones spiral across it. The  and the  show what is
inside — a "Distillate" line, runes and numbers; the Spectacles show it without the Loupe in your hand.

845.content:
**Neighbors on the Wheel get along**:  with ,  with
,  with ,  with 
enter the distillate whole. Compound currents mix with anything without loss.

846.content:
**Opposite Springs clash**:  and ,  and .
A Spring thrown in with its opposite enters only by half, and the other half goes to murk. Whoever went in first stays whole:
the order of throws is part of the craft.

847.content:
**The limit is 64 parts.** Beyond it the Crucible boils over: the excess boils off as murk from the fullest current until
the distillate evens out. Vapor and dark flakes over the rim show at any "Mod Graphics" level — that is the sign to stop.

848.content: Every lost part is half a part of murk in the Crucible's chunk. On murk and mire — the entry .

849.content: The **Patience** aptitude lowers the thrower's loss to clashes and the murk of their things at the Crucible.

850.content:
**To drain the distillate** without losing the water, sneak and use an empty hand on the Crucible: the currents go as murk into
the land (half a part per part), the water stays. An empty Crucible does not answer. A **comparator** by the Crucible tells how
full it is.

851.content:
A Crucible recipe is a **catalyst** (the thing thrown in last) and the currents that must be in the distillate at that moment,
plus heat. If it matches, the recipe's currents leave, the catalyst too, and the result floats up and flies over the rim
(falling back in, it will not dissolve). If not, the catalyst dissolves like any other thing.

852.content:
When several recipes fit one brew, it is always the same one that brews: the most demanding (most currents); among equals —
the one whose currents fill more of the brew; then the one whose leading current comes first on the Wheel (Tide, Strata,
Ember, Gale, Lattice, Fray and on in order of composition). So an extra current changes the result — watch the distillate with
the Loupe and drain what is extra.

853.content:

who has studied its entry — the owner of the thrown thing.

893.content:
Everything in the world of  is a current that has set: stone flows over eons, wood over years, fire in moments. A
**current** is a kind of flux in a thing, and there are forty-two. The Crucible brews from them, Flux Workbench recipes ask for them,
the Conduit strikes with them and Confluence gathers them, and the Wheel tells what combines with what.

894.content:
The four **Springs** are the elements on the Wheel: , , ,
. Each passes into its neighbor: a tide carries silt and strata settle; strata warm and ember is born; ember
lifts the air and gale blows; gale brings rain and the tide comes again.

Lattice gathers, Fray wears away. The crystals in caves grow in exactly these six primal currents.

than was meant to be seen finds their mind falling out of step. Dissonance sends **visions**, and the **Hush** takes it away.
Stillness heals Dissonance: the Still are partly right, and that is their temptation. A fluxionist takes from stillness exactly as
much as is needed, and moves on.

984.content: Dissonance survives death and relogging: it lives in the mind, not the body.

985.content:
Every Dissonance you receive builds **pressure** (Deep — 2 per unit, Dissonance — 1.5, Ripple — 1), and every check adds a share of
what you carry. A vision drops the pressure to a third.

986.content: **A check every 150 seconds.** The countdown is yours and is saved: restarting neither grants nor takes away a check.

987.content:
**The chance of a vision** is pressure / (pressure + 30), no more than three quarters: at pressure 30 it is a half. The **Will**
aptitude adds 6 per rank to the 30: at the fifth, at pressure 30, it is a third.

988.content:
**The severity** of a vision grows with all kinds of Dissonance and with pressure, but heavy Dissonance does not cancel light
visions: a roll falls anywhere up to the ceiling. Things with Dissonance weigh on visions the most. A Calm Visor in a Dam Helm
makes them lighter.

989.content: Under the **Hush** effect the check rolls no dice and pressure does not grow.

1012.content:
A **Figment** is a shadow your out-of-step mind made up: it walks your own path over your last steps. Usually harmless, with heavy
Dissonance it strikes; one blow and it crumbles into ink. Read it with the Loupe to open .

1013.content:
A **Sentinel** is one of the Order's first Vowkeepers, frozen mid-step in the Great Stilling. It strides once a second, in the beat of its
hour: a raised palm falls a second later — step away or get behind it. Its blow takes a second from you — the place holds you fast —
its cry leaves Ripple, and from afar it looses a Still Bolt that flies in jerks to the beat of the hour: step off its path while the
bolt hangs. A vision's Sentinel melts after 30 seconds and drops nothing; in the Stillness Sentinels walk on their own. Read one with
the Loupe — .

1014.content:
The  hears the mind. In hand it ticks evenly while the mind is calm, wavers with Dissonance and stumbles in
advance when a vision is near; in the lower left corner of the screen a small metronome shows a scale behind its glass, filled with
Dissonance by kind. Hover over it in your inventory to see the numbers. A metronome in a hood () shows the
same but stays silent.

1015.content:
Without a Metronome there are quiet signs: when Dissonance grows, ink quivers at the edge of the frame; when a vision is near, ink
breathes in the corners.

1016.content: opens once your Dissonance passes ten.

1017.content:
A pinch of  in a source of **still** water — a pond, a well — hushes it and the neighboring sources of the
same surface, up to nine. A river, or water with flowing water beside it, will not do. Step into the hushed water and keep still:

1018.content: on the third second the **Hush** comes — while it lasts, no visions come;

1019.content: keep standing — Ripple leaves every 4 seconds, Dissonance every 8;

1020.content: one step, and it all begins again.

1021.content:
The  lifts Ripple and a share of Dissonance anywhere, without hush water. Strike it and stand still while it
sounds (6 s): if it plays out, all Ripple and 2 Dissonance leave, under the Hush — 4. A step cuts the chime short. The fork wears
dull — 24 chimes.

1022.content:
The  gives the Hush on the road. Wear it at your neck (a slots mod's necklace slot) or hold it: with
Dissonance, stand still for three seconds — the sachet takes a pinch of Hush Salt from your inventory and gives the Hush for 2 minutes.
It does not lift Dissonance, it only keeps the visions away.

1023.content:
The  keeps hush water around itself — a standing place to lift Dissonance. Pour in a bucket of water and
drop a pinch of salt (up to four): a few seconds later the Font overflows from four spouts, and eight places around it become hush
water. A place counts only if the water has nowhere to run: it needs a floor beneath and a rim beyond the ring. Lay a low stone basin
around the Font, and there will always be hush water in it. One pinch is one overflow; scoop a place out, and the Font refills it
while it has salt.

1033.content: The distillate workshop: vessels and brands, vials, siphons and their fittings, the Gyre, retorts with alembics, the Holding Chamber, Separator, Mixing Vat, Brewing Tower and Abacus, bands, the Atomizer.

1044.content:
The Crucible brews from one cauldron and forgets everything that was in it. The distillate workshop stores currents for later
and carries them by itself: vessels hold, siphons convey, retorts break things into currents with no hands, and the
 brews Crucible recipes for as long as it is fed. The Confluence, the Atomizer, lanterns and other
devices draw from these stores.

1045.content:
A  — glass blown on opaline in rings of old bronze — holds **one current, up to 192 parts**. A siphon
over its neck fills it; a siphon at its side or under its bottom takes from it. Broken by hand, a vessel carries what it holds
with it. Entry — .

1046.content:
**Brand.** A flint and steel on a vessel burns the rune of the current inside into its bronze tag. A branded vessel keeps its
current even when empty: it takes nothing else and calls its own along the siphons. An empty vessel can be branded with an orb —
the orb goes into the tag. An axe scrapes the brand off.

1047.content: **Seal.**  seals the neck: a sealed vessel neither gives nor takes. An axe chips the seal off.

1048.content:
**Puddle.** Tip a vessel over by sneaking with an empty hand — or blow it up — and the distillate lies as a puddle. In ten
seconds it dries, and a quarter of what spilled settles into the land as murk.

1049.content:
**A vessel in hand** pours like a big vial: click it on another vessel, an alembic or a Gyre — it takes that current, as much
as fits, and if there is nothing to take, it gives its own. To place a vessel next to a holder — sneak.

1050.content:
A  keeps its own current and passes what it does not take — its own excess and any other current —
to the vessel below it. Stack spillway vessels on top of each other, and they sort the currents themselves: each gets its own.

1051.content:
A  carries **8 parts** where a siphon cannot reach. A vial on a vessel, an alembic or a Gyre scoops (from a
Gyre — its fullest current, into a filled vial — only its own current); when there is nothing to scoop, it pours out — into a
vessel, a Gyre or a Crucible. You cannot scoop from a Crucible: it is not a store. A vial thrown into a Crucible dissolves together
with what it holds. Entry — .

1052.content:
A  is a glass tube in bronze clamps. Distillate flows along it by itself, like water: **down and level,
never up**. A siphon at its side takes from a Crucible, a siphon over its neck fills a vessel — so the vessel stands lower than
the Crucible. Entry — .

1053.content:
A siphon takes a part only if further down the tube there is a holder that will accept it right now — and gives it straight
there. A brand calls its own current; from a Crucible the fullest of what is awaited leaves first. The nearest holder goes first,
equal ones take turns.

1054.content:
**There are no clogs**: a siphon takes nothing of a current with nowhere to go — its drop trembles at the outlet, and the Loupe on
the siphon says "no receiver". Set a vessel that accepts it, and it flows.

1055.content: Poured into a Crucible from above, distillate mixes by the rules of the Wheel (clashes and the limit — as with thrown things).

1064.content:
Distilling breaks things into currents by itself — no water, no catalyst, no hands. A  is a stone hearth
under a copper gourd: put a thing with currents in it (by hand or a hopper from above) and stoke the hearth (by hand or a hopper
from the side) — the thing breaks down, and its currents rise as vapor into the neck. Entry — .

1065.content:
The currents are caught by  — beaked vessels, **up to four** in a column on the neck. Each current goes
where it already is, otherwise to the first empty one. With nowhere to go, it waits in the retort, and no new thing is taken.
Siphons at the sides take from the alembics.

1066.content:
**Losses**: a plain retort loses **a sixth** of the currents as murk. A  burns in the hearth
four times longer than coal.

1067.content:

nearby catches what is lost **as silt instead of murk** — eight parts per silt (the entry ).

1076.content:
Retorts are reforged on the Flux Workbench: the fluxsteel one from a plain one, the bright one from fluxsteel

1077.content:
The  measures out **12 parts** and gives them all at once when the holder below is empty: with
one siphon you feed a Crucible in portions — it brews, empties and gets the next. While it gives, it takes nothing from above.
Entry — .

1078.content:
The  splits a compound current into its parents: **two parts of the compound — a part of each parent**
(spare Drift becomes Gale and Tide again); a parent that is itself compound splits when it gathers a pair. Siphons at the sides
and below take only Springs and Poles. Nothing is lost or born. Entry — .

1079.content:
The  combines without a Crucible: **two parts of different currents that combine on the Wheel — a part
of the compound**. Opposite Springs merge only if the vat stands lower than both holders they flow from — like a basin of the
Riverbed puzzle; higher, they clash into murk. Entry — .

1080.content:
The Brewing Tower is a self-brewing Crucible: it brews Crucible recipes by itself as long as it is fed by siphon and given
catalysts. It needs neither water nor fire — the chunk's flux heats the brew, and in drained land the tower stands. The milestone
entry — .

1081.content:
**How to get it**: set a Crucible on a  and throw a pinch of quickdust on it — the retort becomes
the firebox, the Crucible the dome. The Crucible's distillate passes into the dome.

1082.content:
**Memory.** Strike the tower with a recipe's catalyst — it remembers the most demanding one you know; sneaking with an empty
hand — it forgets the last one. The tower itself remembers one recipe, every  right against its side —
two more. Potions are taught with the potion itself. The tower brews no creatures: a glint needs a Crucible.

1083.content:
**Feeding.** A siphon over the dome pours only what the remembered recipes need, no more than for two brews. Catalysts go in by
hand or a hopper at the side and top, the brewed things come out by an empty hand or a hopper below.

1084.content:

holds more. A second band does not fit over the first, but a stronger one replaces a weaker one. Entry — .

1099.content: Game enchantments by Confluence — any one at the level you need, with no enchanting-table lottery: how to inscribe, level by opaline, the price doubling per level, conflicts and refusals, Forgotten Enchantments (Mending and others), the table of every inscription, the Flux Sheath, the Unweaving Cloth, Rite Repair.

1109.content:
**Inscription** gives any game enchantment at the level you need — exactly, with no enchanting-table lottery. The same
Confluence altar writes it: the thing under the Heart, the inscription's things on the plinths,
distillate in vessels nearby, a touch of the Conduit. The enchanting table keeps its place: it is cheap and random, the altar exact but
a rite. Entries —  and .

1110.content:
**On the central plinth** — a thing the enchantment fits (as with an anvil: Sharpness — swords and axes, Protection — armor),
**or a book**: a plain one comes out an Enchanted Book, into an Enchanted Book the enchantment joins the others. The book is then put
on the thing with an anvil.

1111.content:
**On the side plinths** — the inscription's level I things (2–4, each enchantment its own; the table below) and **one opaline for
every level above the first**: Sharpness III — flint, flint, an iron ingot and two .

1112.content: **Distillate** — the enchantment's currents in vessels or a Gyre within twelve blocks.

1113.content:
Before you start, the Heart tells what will come out: "Ready: Sharpness III · distillate: 24", the Confluence tier and whether there
is enough calm. A touch of the Conduit begins.

1114.content:
**To start with** — Sharpness I on a sword: two flints, an iron ingot and two parts each of ,
 and . It is a simple Confluence: a bare altar holds it any day or night.

1115.content:
**The level is how many opalines**: 1 + the opalines on the plinths. No higher than the enchantment's top level, and higher than what
the thing already has: Sharpness II rises to IV with three opalines.

1116.content:
**Every level costs twice as much distillate**: Sharpness I — 6 parts, Sharpness V — 96. **Raising** from one level to another costs
only the difference — what was paid for earlier levels is not taken again.

1117.content: **Every other enchantment on the thing** makes the price a quarter higher (weavings do not count here).

1118.content: Reach stones lower the price, as for any Confluence.

1119.content:
A higher level means more things and distillate, and so **a higher Confluence tier**: Sharpness I is simple, Sharpness III mid,
Sharpness V great — it needs weirs and calm stones.

1120.content: Inscription does not get around the rules of the world — the Heart tells you why a thing will not take the inscription:

1121.content:
**conflict**: one thing will not take Sharpness, Smite and Bane of Arthropods together; the protections with each other; Fortune and
Silk Touch; Mending and Infinity; Frost Walker and Depth Strider; Loyalty and Channeling with Riptide; Multishot and Piercing;

1122.content: **above the top**: more opalines than the enchantment has levels;

1123.content: **already there**: the thing has this level or higher;

1124.content: **the wrong thing**: Sharpness on a pickaxe — put a book or a thing the enchantment fits.

1126.content:
**Mending, Frost Walker, Soul Speed, Swift Sneak and Wind Burst** the enchanting table never gives — they are found only in chests and
with villagers. The currents remember them, and the altar writes them the same way, only harder: none of them is ever a simple
Confluence. **Mending is always great**: build the altar with weirs and calm stones.

Compound currents (Bane, Edge, Ward…) come from source things and the . Every inscription is data: in the
Confluence reference.

1177.content:
Besides the game's enchantments, Inscription writes one of its own — the **Flux Sheath** (I–V): a shield over armor, golden hearts of
absorption that fill up again from the land's flux. Each level on a piece of armor or a trinket setting gives half a heart of shield; all
you wear together — no more than ten hearts. The shield tops up half a heart every two seconds, a unit of chunk flux at your feet; in a
murky chunk it does not charge. It is written the same way: the thing in the middle, two pinches of quickdust and an opaline for every
level above the first;  and  in vessels. Entry — .

1178.content:
The  moves one enchantment of a thing into a book whole, at the same level — a grindstone would erase it.
Put the cloth, the thing and a plain book on a crafting table: the cloth pulls out the rarest enchantment (among equally rare — the
highest level) and lays it into the book; the thing keeps the rest. It does not touch curses. Without a book the cloth unravels the
thing's last weaving — and the tension goes with it. The cloth has 24 threads: a transfer costs a thread per level, a forgotten
enchantment twice as much, a weaving three. Entry — .

1179.content:
Confluence mends a worn thing with its own material and leaves everything on it: enchantments, weavings, the Forge's tempering. **The
anvil's work cost does not grow** — a thing the anvil no longer takes ("Too Expensive!") the rite mends again and again. Entry —
.

1180.content:
The thing on the central plinth, pieces of its material on the side ones (iron for iron, diamonds for diamond): **a piece is a quarter
of durability**; the Heart will not take extra pieces.

1181.content:
Distillate by wear: two parts of  per quarter and half the currents of the material itself. An iron pickaxe worn
by a tenth needs three parts, worn by nine tenths nineteen.

1182.content:
It is a simple Confluence; a costly thing with heavy wear makes it mid. A thing with no repair material (a bow, a fishing rod) the rite
does not mend.

1183.content: The altar, calm and weirs: Confluence.

1184.content: Enchantment distillate — from vessels and the Gyre: Vessels, Siphons and Distilling.

1187.content: Omens and cult raids: when and to whom they come, how to answer them and what they reward.

1204.content:
**Omens** are rare changes of the world: once every few days something happens and lasts from a minute to a day. Each comes
where its current is — to murky water, to a living workshop, to Gauge Stones, in a storm or at sunset — and each has **an answer
in your hands** and a reward right at the danger. Witness an omen and it is written into the Codex as its own page of the
 entry: what it is, how to answer it, what it rewards.

1205.content:
**To whom**: an omen comes to a player who has reached its theme — studied an entry, been to a world or met a cult. A newcomer
faces neither the Rounds of the Still nor the Spillover.

1207.content:
**No damage**: an event never breaks a player's blocks, places its own only for a while and in the wild; it may stop devices
but never breaks them. Rewards have a per-player limit — an event is no farm.

1208.content:
**Switches** are world rules: "World events" for omens, "Cult raids" for raids. On a server the operator changes them, in
single player you do (in the rule list when creating the world, or with `/gamerule`).

1209.content:
The three cults of the Reckoners come to whoever has reached their wave — every few days, and only where your own work calls
them: murky water, a tuned stone, a living workshop. A clean neighborhood calls no raid. Two players close together meet one raid. The cults' people are in the Bestiary.

1210.content:
**When**: at night after rain, every 3–6 days, for whoever has studied  — if there is murky water (murk at
a third of the bed or more) within 4 chunks. Murk itself is the invitation.

1211.content:
**What**: 26 blocks from the water a Mirebearer, two Sodden and
a Keener come out and walk to the water; a dark needle of murk rises where they came from, and the
procession bell tolls. The Mirebearer carries a living Mire Hummock on its back and plants it in the water — a new node of mire
will rise there.

1212.content:
**Answer**: clean the water before they arrive — the procession turns back; or strike the whole procession down while the
hummock is still on its back.

1213.content:
**Reward**: the hummock dries into 2–3 , and the Keener sometimes (3 times in 10) drops a
.

1214.content: **When**: by day, every 3–6 days, if a Gauge Stone you have tuned or your own Gauge Post stands within 64 blocks.

1215.content:
**What**: 24 blocks away a Bailiff and two Toll Collectors come out.
The Bailiff walks to the stone and, kneeling for 2 seconds, drives a  into it: the tap drinks the three
chunks around it down to the riverbed.

1216.content:
**Answer**: strike the Bailiff down while he kneels (a strong blow breaks his work) — the Collection is foiled. Too late — break
the tap, and the drunk flux comes back in a surge.

1217.content: **Reward**: a  holding 24–40 of drunk flux — for a beaten Bailiff and from a broken tap.

1218.content:
**When**: at sunset, every 4–7 days, for whoever has studied  or been to the Stillness — at a **living
workshop**: a chunk flux was drawn from in the last minutes that still runs full.

1219.content:
**What**: 20–28 blocks from the workshop a **Still Pane** appears — a sheet of frozen falling water. For twenty seconds it sets,
and the Stillness shows through it. Then a Bellringer, a Vowkeeper and two
Clockbound step out. The Bellringer walks to the middle of the workshop and reads the stone rite for
20 seconds while the others guard him. Once he finishes, a **Halt Stone** rises: in 3 × 3 chunks devices, the Flux Workbench and
the Conduit draw no flux. Nothing breaks, and three blows break the stone — or it crumbles by itself after a day.

1220.content:
**Answer**: thaw the pane — a lit  within 8 blocks or quickwater poured nearby — or break it with
three blows; break the rite with a strong blow (it starts over); strike the squad down before the stone. Walls around the
workshop are an answer too: a Bellringer who can't reach the middle never starts the rite.

1221.content:
**Reward**: a pane thawed or broken before the squad comes out — 1–2 ; a squad struck down before
the stone — 2 more grains and sometimes a . The limit per Rounds is 4 grains and one Rule.

1222.content:
A new skein is born before your eyes — every 5–8 days, for whoever has studied . In clear weather, by living
water (a river, a swamp, a jungle) where the flux runs full and the murk stays below a third of the bed, the streams of nearby
chunks reach for a point above the water and twist like yarn: for a minute they gather, for three minutes the bud grows, in the
last one the threads draw tight — and a skein hangs above the water.

1223.content:
**You decide how it winds**: a full distillate vial poured onto the bud makes its current a native thread — up to three. Murk in
the chunk (a third of the bed or more, for 20 seconds) winds it **murky**, and flux you draw nearby (10 seconds of devices
working) winds it **greedy**; a lumenash nearby sometimes gives a lucent skein.

1224.content: Go farther than 64 blocks and the bud unravels without a trace.

1225.content:
At a clear midnight, every 4–6 days, for whoever has studied , if their tuned Gauge Stone and at least one
more stand within 128 blocks. Yours answers first, then the others in turn: on each, the Marked Tiles light up from the bottom, and
a thread of light runs to the nearest stone that has answered — the network of beds shows to the eye. For two minutes the flux of
the neighborhood flows toward your stone. Read an answering stone with a Loupe — 3 times in 10 it gives a
 (no more than two per Roll Call). There is no danger.

1226.content:
At dawn, every 3–5 days, for whoever has read a race (): for 4 minutes 2–4 schools of
Racefish — fish of light — swim up a clean river nearby. Each school carries its own current — the current
of the place, and sometimes a guest one that never occurs here. Come within 5 blocks and read a school with the Loupe — that is how
rare currents are discovered. Where a school has passed, the river freshens: flux rises, murk falls. The fish can't be caught;
in a murky river the schools turn back.

1227.content:
In a thunderstorm, every 3–5 days, for whoever has studied , if at least three murky chunks lie around.
Every 20–40 seconds a **murk discharge** strikes a murky chunk nearby — without fire, buildings don't burn. 2–3 seconds before
the strike a ring of runes cracks open on the ground: step away (a hit is 3 damage and Silting).

1228.content:
**A game lightning rod** within 32 blocks catches the discharge and **grounds** it: six tenths of the chunk's murk become flux —
the storm cleans your workshop for free.

1229.content:
Into open ground the discharge burns murk away; but where murk is above half the bed and flux is being drawn, a Snarl is born.
A Weir within 8 blocks dampens a strike on a Snarl.

1230.content:
At night, every 4–7 days, for whoever has been to the Lees: the bottom of nearby water breathes out — a **Lees Boil** opens. For
ten minutes it raises the chunk's murk, and Murk Fry rise from the bottom.

1231.content:
**Cap the boil**: a  in the column above the throat (on the bottom and up to two blocks higher)
clogs with silt in half a minute and quenches the boil by a third; a working Purifier in the chunk counts as a grate once a minute.
Three thirds — the boil is capped, and finds float up from the bottom: , ,
sometimes  and a  (no more than 8 things).

1232.content: A shortcut down: a  thrown into the boil raises a Whirlpool to the Lees at once.

1233.content:
A large omen, every 7–12 days, if someone in the world has passed into the Quickstream: a race of the Quickstream spills over the
edge of its bed and **flows across the sky for 8 minutes** above their neighborhood — a ribbon 6–10 blocks wide, from one edge of
the sky to the other.

1234.content:
Under it (within 16 blocks of its trace on the ground) the bed is 1.4 times as deep, murk is carried away, and **the current of
place is the race's current**: the Flux Workbench pays with it, Current Seeds grow by it, skeins wind threads twice as often.
The current can be any, guest ones (Soul, Tempo, Echo, Halo) more often.

1235.content:
The race **carries** like the races of the Quickstream: climb up with a Grapnel or a Vane Mantle and ride it; whoever it carries in
the last 10 seconds is set down gently. Schools of Racefish swim along it — read them.

1236.content:
There is no threat: it is a gift, but a short one — hurry to forge, and to fill a  and a
.

1237.content:
A large omen, every 7–12 days, at sunset, if someone in the world has seen the Stillness. For three minutes the world falls into
its beat: the sun stands at the horizon, stars show by day, the light stays that of sunset, and **the flux of the world neither flows
nor refills** — use what is there. Near every player 1–3 Stilled Figures () appear.

1238.content:
**Answer**: a  within 8 blocks or quickwater — the figure finishes its step: it speaks a line and
leaves a , and every third one rises as a Laggard. A pickaxe breaks one into
1–2 still grains. The untouched ones crumble once the sun moves on.

1239.content: The limit is 4 grains and one Still Memory. It is a second way to still grains besides Snarls.

1240.content:
A rare omen, every 8–12 days, from dawn to dawn, if someone in the world has met . The Tollkeepers on the
Quickstream spin the Toll Wheel with the flux they have drunk, and the Springs of every place stand one step further along the
Wheel: Tide reads as Strata, Strata as Ember, Ember as Gale, Gale as Tide. The Poles and compound currents, items and creatures
stay the same.

1241.content:
Use it: a Flux Workbench recipe and Current Seeds that lacked a Spring of place will come together today. Or wait it out —
a Brimming Jug by the river stays silent for the day.

1242.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

1243.content:
A small omen, every 3–5 days, by day, for whoever has studied : a Snagling Peddler with a laden Driftback
comes out to you and trades with anyone for a day — saplings and herbs of faraway places, a rare find and a map to a ruin. More in
the guide The Snaglings.

1244.content:
**The Murkflow** — in the Lees, every 25–40 minutes spent there: a wall of murk moves along the bottom past
you (a block a second). Whoever it covers gets Silting, and chunks on its way get 3 murk each. It goes around the Bright Shallows
and any chunk with a working Purifier. 3–5 things of the bottom tumble in its crest — snatch them with a blow of a
 (no more than 5).

1245.content:
**The Living Minute** — in the Stillness, for whoever has spent 30–45 minutes there, outside a Thaw
Lantern's circle: the Stillness moves for a minute. Within 48 blocks the bed is 16: the Conduit, the Flux Workbench and devices work
without their own store, still skeins give up their threads. The Sentinels wake, and 6–9  fall from the
sky — gather them and get away.

1285.content:
Crystals grow in the six primal currents — the four Springs and the two Poles; each glows its own color and rings softly when
touched. A broken crystal drops shards, and their colors tell them apart.

1286.content:
is a cheap recipe on the ordinary crafting table: shards of the four Springs, an antimony regulus and
redstone. It needs no entries — the Codex comes before everything else.

1287.content:
A pinch on a bookshelf (any, the chiseled one too) — the shelf crumbles, and  rises from a
vortex of currents. Knowledge lives in you, not in the book: a lost Codex is woken again from another shelf and forgets nothing.
A few seconds after the awakening a line above the hotbar tells you how to open the book.

1288.content:
The first entry, , is open from the start: press Study. The Codex opens itself on an entry you can
already study, and once you know enough for a new one, a line above the hotbar says Ready to study.

1289.content: Entries ask for knowledge, and only the  brings it. Its recipe is in the first entry.

1290.content:
Hold the Loupe on anything — a block, a thing, a creature, the air — for a second and a half. The first reading of a thing gives
**notes** to the chapters its currents lean toward, and a current you have never met is **revealed** and brings notes of Basics.
Read everything: grass, water, ore, animals, your own tools. How the Loupe works is in the Loupe guide.

The  comes later: its entry stands behind Fluxsteel from the Crucible. The Flux Workbench pays for
a recipe with the flux of your chunk — from then on, where you work matters.

1304.content: **By a river.** A river's riverbed is one of the deepest in the overworld, and the neighbors top the flux up quickly.

1305.content: **With a willow nearby.** A living weeping willow by water raises its chunk's riverbed 1.35 times.

1306.content: **Away from murk.** A murkcap in a cave is a sign the flux there has stagnated: plant a lumenash beside it, not a workshop.

1307.content:
Rough work leaves murk: remelting in the Crucible, a broken confluence, a cheap lens. Murk above a third of the riverbed grows
mire. Watch the murk number by the Loupe's crosshair — the Murk and Mire guide.

1309.content: Currents and the Wheel — the language of the whole craft.

1324.content:
The  does everything a crafting table does and, on top of that, **flux recipes**: device parts,
devices and the fluxionist's gear. They are paid for with the flux of the land under the workbench and with the currents of the
place. The Codex chapter is Artifice, its first entry  (after the
Crucible's fluxsteel).

1325.content:
A pinch of  on a plain crafting table — a simple use, no Shift: the oak darkens, veins of flux run
across it, bronze binds its corners, and the crafting grid becomes the Wheel of Currents. The Flux Workbench has no recipe of
its own. Waking needs no knowledge; recipes ask for it.

1326.content:
In the middle of the Wheel is a 3×3 grid, around it **six shard sockets**: the four Springs in Wheel order and the two Poles,
Lattice on top and Fray below. The socket of a current that flows in the place glows in its color.

1327.content:
On the right — the bowl where the thing appears, and the vessel of **the flux of the place** (the same as the Loupe's): what the
craft will take flickers on the flux itself.

1328.content:
What you lay out stays on the workbench when you walk away. The things are shared by everyone who opened the window, but the
result is by the opener's knowledge: whoever has not studied the entry sees the thing pale and the entry's name as a line.

1329.content: Plain crafting-table recipes the Flux Workbench makes **for free**.

1330.content: A flux recipe asks for things, **flux** and **currents of the place** (Springs and Poles only).

1331.content:
**A current is free if it flows in the place** — as the Loupe reads the air.  — almost everywhere,
 — by water, in forests and in snow,  — in mountains, caves and deserts,
 — in deserts, forests and the Nether,  — in deserts, mushroom lands and the End,
 — only in snow.

1332.content:
**What the place lacks, a shard gives** from the socket of its current — one per craft. But such craft is rougher: **murk +1**
settles in the land. With neither the current nor a shard, the window names the current in red.

1333.content:
**Flux** is taken from the workbench's chunk, but never below **the bed floor** — a tenth of the bed. What is taken comes back by
itself — from the bed and from neighbors: by a river the workbench hardly runs dry, in a desert it does fast.

1334.content: **Drought**: whatever is missing up to the price, shards from any socket give — **8 flux each**, clean, without murk.

1335.content:
Recipes cost 4 to 60 flux: expensive craft sooner or later calls for a Catchment. How flux flows and where it is plentiful —
Flux and Murk of the World.

1336.content:
The **fluxionist's garb** and the **Finesse** aptitude (−6% flux per rank) make craft cheaper — together never below half;
they do not save the shards paid for the place's currents.

A  lights dark corners by itself: at night its fireflies fly out and settle as little lights where
it is dark, and return at dawn. Made from a bottled glint it is cheaper — no prism and no dust ().

1345.content: Float lanterns are light on water in sixteen colors; by a Confluence stream they calm its turbulence ().

1347.content:
A  next to the Flux Workbench gives it **the flux of nine chunks instead of one**: it takes more from
the full ones and dries the surroundings evenly instead of draining the nearest piece to the bottom ().

1348.content:
A  is a store for drought: it skims the top of the flux while the land is full and gives it back when
craft, a device or the Conduit drain it. The workbench draws on the reservoirs of its land right after the land itself. A broken one
gives its store to the land ().

1349.content:
A  charges things that hold a store of flux: the Grapnel, the Flux Trowel and Flux Ruling Pen, the
Guiding Glint. The basin fills with flux like a font, but never below the bed floor; a thing rises over it and drinks. A siphon at
its side also feeds things that run on distillate — the Prism Rod ().

1350.content:
**Gear Charge**: the mod's armor holds a charge, and its features spend it. The "Gear Charge" row above the armor bar shows cells
per piece; living land tops up worn pieces slowly (a unit every four seconds while flux is above the bed floor), the basin in seconds.
In detail — Gear and Gear Charge.

1351.content:
**Fluxsteel tools** cut like diamond and work faster in full flux (and drag in drained land); a sword strikes more often there.
The **armor** speeds up devices nearby and builds static as you walk — in the full set sneak twice and it strikes three nearest
enemies with arcs ().

1352.content:
The **fluxionist's garb** of  barely protects but saves flux: the coat an eighth, the trousers a little
less, the shoes less still; Diviner's Spectacles too. In total — no more than half the price. The flux thread also dampens magic
(potions of harming, witches) and keeps murk off. It dyes like leather armor ().

1353.content:
A  has six pockets of 128 shards, one per Spring and Pole; the Flux Workbench takes from it by
itself ().

1354.content:
A  is 54 slots always with you; it opens with the "Open Lined Satchel" key; the workshop takes from
it as from your hands (). A second lining by Confluence doubles it.

1355.content:

a knot costs chunk flux ().
