1359.content: Flux and Murk of the World

1360.content: The flux and murk of every chunk: a place's riverbed, how flux flows and refills, the riverbed floor, the willow and the lumenash, where to set a workshop.

1365.content: The willow gathers, the lumenash cleanses

1370.content:
Flux is what a fluxionist works with: the Flux Workbench, the Conduit, Confluence and devices draw it from the land around them.
Where the flux runs full, work goes on; where it is drained, work stops. Every chunk has its own store of flux and its own murk,
and both show by the Loupe's crosshair: **Flux N / M** and **murk**.

1371.content: The **riverbed** is how much flux a chunk holds when left alone: the second number by the crosshair. It depends on the place:

1380.content:
| Place                    | Riverbed |
| ------------------------ | -------- |
| snowy places, the Nether | 45       |

1384.content:
That is the middle: each chunk has its own riverbed, from three quarters to five quarters of this number. Places from other mods
without their own tags are read by their climate. 's own places hold their own riverbeds — up to 160.

1385.content:
**It seeps to the neighbors**: every second a chunk gives each of its four neighbors 6 % of the difference in fullness — from full
to empty, like water through sand. Rivers, valleys and Gauge Stones are its beds: along them it runs faster.

1386.content: **It refills by itself**: every second a chunk gains a hundredth of what it lacks up to its riverbed.

1387.content: **An overfull chunk spills**: a chunk filled above five quarters of its riverbed gives the surplus to its neighbors twice as fast.

1388.content:
So a chunk drained at once among full ones is 90 % full again in seven or eight seconds, while a chunk held right at the floor
keeps giving for a long time — about 13 flux a second: the neighbors two or three chunks around feed it. A device that drinks less
than a couple of units a second holds up anywhere.

1389.content:
The lowest tenth of the riverbed is the **floor**: the Flux Workbench and gear top-ups take only what lies above it. Devices
cannot dry a chunk below the floor: the land stays alive. What the land lacks, the Flux Workbench takes from the shards in its
sockets.

1390.content:
Flux drawn roughly does not vanish — it stagnates into **murk**: in Crucible remelting, in a broken confluence, in a cheap lens.
Murk does not seep to the neighbors but settles where it was spilled.

1391.content:
**Murk takes the place of flux**: a chunk refills only up to "riverbed minus murk". A murky workshop is not just dirty — it has
less flux.

1392.content: **Above a third of the riverbed**, settled murk grows **mire**; above half, if flux keeps being drawn, a Snarl may rise.

1393.content: Murk flakes in the air show even without the Loupe: the murkier the surroundings, the more of them.

1394.content: How to clear murk and what to do about mire is in Murk and Mire.

1395.content:
**A weeping willow** by water — a willow trunk in the part of the chunk where or under which there is water, with its leaves or
strands in the chunk — raises its chunk's riverbed **1.35 times**. Even the poorest chunk with a willow holds no less than the
place's average. One willow per chunk: a second adds nothing; a felled trunk puts the willow out at once.

1396.content:
**A lumenash** with living leaves turns its chunk's murk into flux — **0.02 a second per trunk**, up to three trunks per chunk.
One lumenash clears a plains chunk from the mire threshold in about 15 minutes: it keeps a tidy workshop clean but does not save a
rough one. Every few seconds sparks of Gleam flash over a cleansing lumenash.

1397.content:
**Mire in the riverbed** — silted blocks where there is water — lowers the chunk's riverbed by a fifth: a workshop by a river has
reason to clean up.

1398.content:

| -------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| by a river, a swamp, in a jungle | in a desert, on a mountain |

1402.content: **The Nether** and **the End** have riverbeds of their own (45 and 18); climate is not read there.

1403.content: **The Stillness** is a world where nothing flows: there is no flux in it, and devices run on what you bring along.

1404.content: **The Lees** are the bottom of the flux: murk flows there, and every chunk's flux is only its own.

1405.content:
Now and then the world changes the flux for a while. The **Roll Call** of Gauge Stones on a clear midnight gathers the surrounding
flux to your workshop, the **Spillover** of the Quickstream deepens the riverbed under the race 1.4 times for eight minutes, a **Murk
Storm** strikes murky chunks, and the Tollkeepers' **Toll Collection** dries three chunks around your Gauge Stone to the floor.
An omen you witness is written into .

1411.content: Weapons, armor and trinkets: a role instead of "the strongest", abilities and mastery, the set move, Gear Charge, the bond of trinkets, Tuning Pegs.

1423.content:
has no "most powerful armor": every thing has its own **role** — the case where it beats the others. The next stage of the
path brings a different role, not bigger numbers: armor of different metals is for different cases, not a ladder.

1424.content:
A thing's tooltip is short: a weapon shows its role, ability and mastery; armor its set, strong side and **flaw** (a real one, it
gets in the way in play); a trinket its slot and action. Hold **H** over a thing in any window with slots: a bar fills under the
line, and the details screen opens — a model you turn with the mouse (armor shows the whole set on a stand or on you), numbers, the
ability at the current mastery, every level, the set's thresholds, the lore and where to get it. The key can be changed in the
controls.

1425.content:
A weapon has an **ability** of its own: on right-click, or on hit with a chance. The cooldown starts only if the ability worked:
with nobody to strike, no cooldown is spent.

1426.content: Abilities strike foes, not everyone: villagers, pets and companions are left alone.

1427.content: **Readiness shows on the model itself**: a part that grows back with the cooldown.

1428.content:
A weapon gathers experience from victories: for every foe it slays, a fifth of the foe's health rounded up (a zombie — 4, a tough
master — hundreds). Experience and level live **in the item itself** and pass with it from hand to hand. There are three to five
levels: each strengthens the ability noticeably, the last changes it (a fan instead of a line, a second leap). The level shows in the
tooltip, all levels on the details screen.

too. Each set has one to three noticeable things of its own, true to its meaning.

1438.content:
Two sneak presses in a row (the second within 8 ticks) perform the worn set's **move**. With a movement key held, it is a move with
motion, if the set has one (Midstep, Unstoppable Rush); otherwise a move in place (Open Spillway, Mute Toll, Taken Time,
Rime Shroud, Pattern Flare, Static Discharge). Moves in place come with a full set of three or four pieces. Not ready — a line
"…in 6 s"; ready again — a ring of motes in the set's color at your feet. The gesture does not count in flight, with the vane
spread, in a saddle or with a window open.

1439.content: Armor is silent: moves and features make no sound — only particles, rings and glow.

1440.content:
The features of 's armor pay with **a charge of flux** held by the pieces themselves. Above the vanilla armor bar, left over the
hearts, stands the **Gear Charge** row — ten opaline flasks in brass, split between the worn things: you can see which one is running
dry.

1447.content:
**A set's store is its worn pieces**: it spends from the least full non-empty piece and refills the emptiest — pieces run dry one
at a time.

1448.content:
**An empty store — the features sleep**: the armor itself remains — protection, toughness, the set's bonuses and its flaws.
Freshet Garb's flight, its repair in water, sight and breathing need no charge.

1449.content: **Too little charge — no deed**: a move refuses with a line "not enough charge — 1 of 3".

1450.content:
**Top-up**: a living chunk tops up worn armor by itself — **0.25 flux a second** (a full set from empty in 4–6 minutes), only
above the riverbed floor. A drained chunk, a Halt Stone and the Stillness do not top up: go there with a full store. Faster are
the  (4 a second), the  and the .

1451.content:
The charge travels with the thing: the basin, death, the anvil and the smithing table keep it. A new piece is full; repairing two
pieces on a crafting table adds their charges, up to the limit.

1452.content:
Each piece's tooltip says what costs how much ("Flux charge: N / M" and what spends it). A rule of thumb: a move made once every
6–60 seconds costs 2–6; something that lasts, a unit every minute or two; a blow taken by a vow or by rime, a unit.

1453.content:
Rings, necklaces, belts and charms go into the slots of a **slots mod**: on Fabric — Trinkets, on NeoForge — Curios (or Trinkets).
A slots mod is optional: without it  runs, but a trinket cannot be worn — its tooltip names the mod it needs. Without a slots
mod the Diviner's Spectacles go in the helmet slot, and the  is held in hand. Trinkets are silent: only an
action you perform yourself makes a sound (the dash of the ).

1454.content:
A trinket with an action **bonds** with its owner: it drinks the flux of the deed it was made for, and with every level it strings a
**bead** onto its cord. Experience comes only while it is worn in a real slot.

1455.content: Bond 1–10; level N → N+1 costs N of the thing's steps (a step is how many of its deeds the first level takes: 15 dashes, 30 charge…).

1456.content: Every level after the first gives a bead; a bead goes into one of the action's numbers (reach, cooldown, share…).

1457.content: At **bond 5** — a twist: a second action or a change to the first.

1458.content: **Untying the beads** frees them all for experience levels, a level per bead. Experience, level and twist stay.

1474.content: A Spring tincture is a current's guise for three minutes: four Spring guises and three compound ones, weaknesses, kindred and foreign places, price and end.

1482.content:
A Spring tincture makes you its current for three minutes: Gale leaps and glides, Ember does not burn and swims in lava, Strata
cannot be moved, Tide swims and breathes under water. Each guise has two or three clear advantages and one honest weakness. The entry
is  in the Alchemy chapter, after Unheard-of Potions: 5 notes of Alchemy and a reading of a glint, a blaze or
a breeze.

1483.content:
The Crucible brews a tincture over **gentle heat**: Brew 2, a Spring 4 and Soul 2, the bottle last. Without the studied entry a
tincture does not brew, and it leaves no murk: this is craft, not a rare potion.

1484.content:
Drink it like a potion; the bottle stays. A guise lasts **3 minutes** in an ordinary place and survives leaving the game; it ends
with death. The same tincture over its own guise gives full time again (it does not stack beyond three minutes). Milk does not lift
a guise.

1493.content: **Tide and Strata** are neighbors without a compound current: the guise simply changes to the new one.

1494.content:
**Opposites** — Tide and Ember, Strata and Gale — **clash**, as in the Crucible: the guise tears apart in a cloud of steam or
dust, the tincture is lost, murk goes into the chunk and Ripple into your eyes. Settling begins.

1495.content: A compound guise keeps only its own two tinctures (they renew its time): any third Spring is the opposite of one of its parents.

1496.content: The Poles — Lattice and Fray — give no guises: they are directions, not elements, and there is nothing to embody.

1497.content:
A guise grows stronger where its current is the place's current, and wanes where its opposite is. The place is what the Loupe reads
in the air plus what you stand in: water and rain are Tide, lava and fire are Ember, stone overhead deep underground is Strata, height
under the open sky is Gale.

| **foreign** — or chunk flux below a quarter of the riverbed | numbers ×0.6, the time runs twice as fast |

1501.content:
Tide is kindred by rivers and seas, in water and rain, foreign in deserts and the Nether. Ember is kindred in the Nether, deserts and
lava, foreign in rain. Strata is kindred in caves, mountains and underground, foreign high in the sky. Gale is kindred on peaks,
foreign underground. The Stillness is foreign to all: no flux flows there. Fire immunity, breathing, "cannot be moved" and the
weaknesses do not depend on the place.

1502.content:
In the lower left corner is the **guise medallion**: the current's rune, a time arc around the rim and three place notches (all lit —
kindred, one — ordinary, dimly flickering — foreign); below it, the time and a word for the place. A change of place brings a short
mod line: "grows stronger: its current is here" or "wanes: a foreign place". A shell of the guise flows over the body — wind streams,
cracks of heat, malachite veins, rippling water — and everyone nearby sees it. The first guise of your life is a small celebration:
the current's rune rises over your head.

1503.content:
While a guise lasts, it takes **0.1 flux a second** from the chunk beneath you (about 18 over three minutes). Where the flux is
below a quarter of the riverbed, the guise has nothing to breathe — it wanes.

1504.content: **Settling**: after any guise ends, no new tincture can be drunk for 30 seconds — "the current in you has not settled yet".

1505.content: **A chain**: tincture after tincture for more than 6 minutes in a row — Ripple 1 for every minute beyond. Settling breaks the chain.

1569.content: The Sounding Lead and the Whirlpool

1581.content:
**The Lees** is the world at the bottom of the murk. You go there for **niello** — a pure store of Murk — for **Lees Shells**
with pearls, for the life of the bottom and for the Great Dam. Stagnant flux does not vanish: it settles — through the flux,
like silt through water, all the way down: layer upon layer, all the murk the fluxionists have spilled since the Great Stilling
lies there, and the living mire on it is ground, not blight. Everything is turned around here: **murk flows, and the only flux is
your own**. The Codex entry is ; it waits for you to read a Snarl.

1582.content: The door to the Lees is murky water itself. The  is made at the Flux Workbench:

1583.content: Throw the lead into water like a snowball. The water will do if:

1584.content: it is at least **three blocks** deep, with a surface of at least **3 × 3** clean water sources and no water above it;

1585.content:
the murk of the chunk is at least **half the riverbed**; by a **Mire Shrine** the water need not be murky: a Whirlpool rises in
clean water there too and never fades;

1586.content: there is no other Whirlpool in that surface, and the world is neither the Lees nor the Stillness.

1587.content:
If the water will not do, the lead floats back up as an item, and the mod tells you why (for clean water, how much murk there is
and how much is needed). If it will, the lead sinks for five seconds, the cord runs down knot by knot, and a **Whirlpool** rises
in the middle of the surface. It cannot be scooped with a bucket or broken. The Whirlpool drinks the murk of its chunk: cleanse
the chunk below a third of the riverbed and it fades, and the lead floats back. The lead always comes back — after a refusal, a
throw that missed the water or a broken surface.

1588.content:
Step into the Whirlpool: it spins you and pulls you down. Stay in it for **2 seconds** — your view spins faster and faster, murk
closes in from the edges, the circle of the surface above shrinks and dims, and the "Down to the Lees" screen sets you on the
bottom. Step out early and the count starts over.

1589.content:
The Lees lies **right under the water**: the same x and z. Over the Ooze Basins the passage looks for the nearest shore of
another biome within 160 blocks.

1590.content: On the bottom a **Rising Column** meets you — a column of pale bubbles. The same Whirlpool always leads to the same Column.

1591.content:
The passage only touches what is natural and only where you may build: it never cuts into someone's house on the bottom — it
sets the Column beside it.

1592.content: Every dive costs the Whirlpool two murk of its chunk.

1593.content: Your first dive is a reading for the Codex and **Deep Dissonance** 1 ("the weight of the bottom"; the Stillness gives 3).

1594.content:
Stand in the Rising Column for **3 seconds**: bubbles of light burst up from below, the "Up toward the light" screen, and you
come out on the shore by your Whirlpool, facing it — even if it has faded. No shore — onto the surface; no water any more — onto
the ground above that spot. **A Column remembers its own**: it lifts only those who came down through it — you cannot walk along
the bottom to someone else's Column and come out in their home.

1595.content:
**The riverbed is 4**, the smallest in the world: flux here is whatever you make (a Purifier, a lumenash, a skein). Flux does
not flow between the chunks of the Lees.

1596.content:
**Bed murk**: every chunk holds its own one and a half riverbeds of murk (6) and pulls back toward it; murk flows from chunk to
chunk the way flux does above. A cleansed chunk fills again — from its neighbors and from the bed. The Bright Shallows have no
bed murk.

1597.content: **The mire stands**: on untouched bottom it does not grow; there are no Snarls in the Lees — this is the bottom itself.

1598.content: **Weight 0.6**: you jump higher and fall slower and softer.

1599.content:
**You cannot sleep** or set a spawn point; there is no weather and no clouds. Days pass as in the Overworld: the window of light
dims toward night, but the bottom never goes black — night here is lilac.

1600.content:
**Air above the ooze**: over the Ooze Basins, less than five blocks above the surface, the air thins as under water — a full
breath lasts 15 seconds. **Under a vault the air holds**, as in a diving bell: in a cave, a room, an alcove three blocks deep,
under a roofed bridge. A Bubbleback's bubbles give you a breath too.

1601.content:
**The Murkflow**: every 25–40 minutes a wall of murk sweeps along the bottom near a player — it adds murk to every chunk in its
path and silts whoever it engulfs. It passes around the Bright Shallows and the chunk of a working Purifier; snatch things from
its crest with a Pike Pole.

1602.content:
The Lees has no sky: overhead is the underside of the surface, as seen from the bottom of a pond. In the middle is a **window**
to the sky of the world, a circle with a trembling rim and a bright line along it; toward the rim the sky turns bluer and sinks
into the depth, in the middle it is warm light. A fine mesh of glints runs over the surface, and narrow slanting rays fall from
the window. The window brightens and dims with the days of the Overworld.

1603.content:
| Biome      | What is there                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Silt Flats | dunes of Bedsilt, half-buried things of the world: broken columns, fish ribs, jars, a cauldron, an anchor chain with a weight |

1604.content:
| Biome        | What is there                                            |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mire Thicket | a forest of Mirebound Logs, growths, threads, mire vents |

1605.content:

| The Still Bed | rimed silt, cold slate-blue light, frozen plumes of murk and hanging flakes — the Stillness lies just beneath |

1608.content:
The ground of the world is , the soil is : your feet sink a little below its
top. There is no lava. The skeins of the Lees are murky; in the Bright Shallows they are lucent.

1609.content:
A clean camp is a place where you can live and work on the bottom. A single Purifier in the middle of the mire will not cope:
every chunk pulls back toward its bed murk, and the neighbors fill a cleansed one. A camp of **3 × 3 chunks** is held together:
**three or four**  with grates, and lumenash trees. Where the murk drops below a third of the riverbed,
the mire recedes into silt and stone, and  breaks through the revived silt — the glowing grass of the
bottom, the sign of a camp. Glowbloom planted up above does not spread — only on the bottom.

1610.content: The life of the bottom tells you where it is clean and where it is dangerous (the entry ):

1611.content:
**Murk Fry** swim in shoals through the depth, glow with murk and gather where there is more of it. They scatter from light in
your hand and from lanterns, and they leave a clean camp.

1612.content:
**The Silt Ray** lies in the Bedsilt: a mound of silt, two warm eyes and the tip of a barb show. Come closer than three blocks
(sneaking — one and a half) and it leaps in an arc and stings: Silting and Slowness for a few seconds. On stone it cannot hide.

1613.content:
**The Bubbleback** is big and peaceful: it eats Mire Threads and breathes out bubbles — whoever stands in them can breathe even
above the basins. It follows Clearwort held in hand. The Sunken hunt Bubblebacks.

1614.content:
**The Silt Delver**, a big crayfish of the bottom, plows the silt with its claws and every few minutes turns up a find: a
concentrate, a bone, an Antimony Flake, a Lees Shell, now and then Niello or a Flux Pebble, on the Still Bed Still Grains. It
never digs the same spot twice — follow it. It never attacks first, but touch it and it pinches.

1615.content: All of them are in the Bestiary.

1616.content:
is murk pressed by the depth into black stone with a violet sheen. Its veins lie in the Layerstone,
larger deeper down; it needs an iron pickaxe. In the Crucible a piece of niello is eight shares of Murk with no grime and no other
currents: a Murk Flask is brewed and a Murk Fumer fed with it without muddying the workshop.

1617.content:
The  is niello in a speculum setting for the Conduit. The murk of a dry lens, a weak cast and a rough
draw goes into the inlay, not into the chunk — up to sixteen. Rinse a full one: drop the Conduit into a stream for five seconds.

1618.content: **Bedsilt** dropped into running water for five seconds washes into Silt, with a 1 in 16 chance of a current shard per block.

1619.content:
The  grows a pearl out of murk — only on bare silt where the murk is at least a third of the riverbed.
Take it with silk touch and the pearl stays: a shell with a ripe pearl is the best calm stone for a Confluence altar (+8).

1620.content:
The  drops from a ray slain by a player in half the fights. Two barbs and Silt give the **Sting**
weaving: a hit silts, and a hit on a silted foe silts deeper.

1621.content:
**The Sunken Hamlet** — stilt huts of the Sunken around a pool of Mire Ooze, a Mire Idol on a platform, nets of thread. Sodden,
a Keener and a Mirebearer guard it; the barrels hold niello, shells and now and then a Sunken Lament.

1622.content:
**The Sunken Barge** — a Reckoner measuring barge dug stern-first into the silt of the Silt Flats, listing to one side. Its
cabin holds a log and a barrel of Records, its hold the Reckoners' crates and jars.

1623.content:
**The Great Dam** closes a channel of ooze from shore to shore. The guardian sleeps on the crest; inside lie galleries, water
chambers with sluice puzzles and hidden rooms; the vault under the crest is cast on every side and cannot be dug into. Each
chamber pit has two wheels: one lets some spans in, the other lets them out; the gate rises when the water stands at the lit mark,
and the lectern of the chamber names the wheels' measures. The dry bed under the dam lies in the thin air of the basin: breathe in
the alcoves under its body.

1627.content: Bestiary — the life of the bottom and the Sunken.

1635.content: The Loupe and the Diviner's Spectacles

1638.content:
The  is the only instrument that brings the Codex knowledge. With it you read the currents of things, scout
the flux of the land and catch the hour in the sky. Its recipe is in the first Codex entry; opaline for the glass lies deep
underground.

1639.content:
Take the Loupe in hand and hold it on a target: after **a second and a half** (30 ticks) it reads it. The reach is **5 blocks**.
Anything with flux in it can be read:

1640.content:
| Target             | What it gives                                              |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| a block or a thing | the thing's currents; a block and its item are one reading |

1641.content:
| Target     | What it gives                                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| a creature | the creature's currents; for some, by their birthplace |

1642.content:
| Target                             | What it gives                                             |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| the air (looking into empty space) | **The flow of a place** — the currents of where you stand |

1643.content:
| Target                         | What it gives             |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| an omen of the world, an event | its own page in the entry |

1644.content:
| Target              | What it gives                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| the sky at its hour | and the other Marks — after the entry |

1645.content:
A first reading is a **New reading**: the card by the crosshair shows the currents and their numbers, how many notes came and to
which chapters, and which current was revealed. A repeat is just a **Reading**: the Codex remembers what it has seen, and the line
Already in your Codex says so. A thing with a current new to you teaches a second time too: two skeins of one kind can hold
different threads.

1646.content: Each current of a thing gives notes to its chapter — half its number, at least one; at most 12 from one thing in total.

1647.content: A current you have never met is **revealed** and brings 3 notes of Basics.

1648.content:
| Chapter | Its currents                     |
| ------- | -------------------------------- |
| Basics  | and every newly revealed current |

1655.content:
Short of notes for a chapter? Read things with its currents. The **Intellect** aptitude adds to the notes of first readings
(Aptitudes).

1656.content:
A thing in a chest need not be taken out. In any window with slots — inventory, chest, furnace, creative inventory — pick up the
Loupe on the cursor and hold it over a slot: after the same second and a half the thing is read just as in the world, with notes
and revelations. Move the cursor away, put the Loupe down or close the window, and the reading breaks off.

1657.content:
The water you swim in does not stop the Loupe's ray: through it you read fish, squid, seagrass, coral, the sand of the bottom.
If nothing is within five blocks, the water itself is read — look into open water. Standing waist-deep on the bottom, you look at
the surface from above and read the water, as on the shore. A waterlogged block (grass, kelp, a stair) is always read as the block.

1658.content:
While the Loupe is in hand, the crosshair shows **Flux N / M** of your chunk — how much living flux there is now and how deep the
riverbed is — and **murk**, if any has settled. Look for places where the flux runs full: work goes easier there. If the murk
grows, work more gently or move the workshop. What the numbers mean is in Flux and Murk of the World.

1659.content:
On a device the Loupe tells you its state: what a Crucible or a vessel holds, whether a siphon flows and where, what a Purifier
lacks, how tight a Snarl is wound. On a block that quickdust will wake, it names under the block what sleeps inside.

1661.content:
**The Loupe in hand** — reading and scouting: the chunk's flux and murk, the riverbed, the currents of whatever you look at,
readings with notes.

1662.content:
** on your head** — only what a device with currents inside holds when you look at it:
the Crucible's distillate, vessels, siphons. No chunk flux, no currents of ordinary blocks, no readings — the spectacles do not
get in the way as you run about the workshop. With a slots mod they can be worn in an accessory slot, without one — in the
helmet slot.

1663.content:
The **Acuity** aptitude adds a block of reach and 3 ticks of speed per rank: at the fifth the Loupe reads from 10 blocks in
0.75 s — in the world, in a window slot and in the sky.

1664.content: Currents and the Wheel — what exactly the Loupe reads.

1665.content: The Codex of Currents — where the notes go.

1666.content: Flux and Murk of the World — the numbers by the crosshair.

1668.content: What holds for every device: the land's flux as their energy, the bed floor, the Catchment and Flux Reservoir, siphons instead of wires, the Flux Mill and other mods' energy, hoppers and pipes, windows and the Loupe, block builds, owners and guests.

1675.content:
A device is a block of the mod with its own job: the Crucible, vessels and siphons, retorts, the Flux Workbench, the Forge, the
Molder, the Confluence altar, the Lens Grinder, totems and mirrors. Here is what is true for all of them at once. All devices by
group, with models and Codex entries, are in the Devices reference.

1676.content:
The mod has no "energy" of its own in units. **Devices draw the flux of the piece of land they stand on**: flux flows through chunks
by itself, every chunk has its own bed — how much flux the land holds.

1677.content:
**The bed floor** is a tenth of the bed: nothing draws below it. On drained land a device waits, and the Loupe and window say why
("The land has nothing to pay", "Dry").

1678.content: One unit for the whole mod: chunk flux, flux in a Reservoir and charge in an item are counted as one number.

1679.content:
A **** next to a Flux Workbench lets crafting draw from the nine chunks around, each by how full it is:
the area dries evenly.

1680.content:
A **** stores the top of the flux while the land is full (above 0.9 of the bed) and gives it back
in a drought (below 0.6); it holds 240. A broken jar returns its store to the land.

1681.content: A **** charges items with the land's flux.

1682.content:
A living Snarl nearby (within 8 blocks of its seam) carries off up to a quarter more with every draw, and the Flux Workbench,
Crucible and Conduit misfire now and then.

1683.content:
Set up the workshop by a river and willows, spread the hungry devices over different chunks. What the bed and murk are — the
Flux and Murk of the World guide.

1684.content:
**Flux is not carried by wires** — it flows through the land by itself. Between devices flows **distillate**: siphons carry it
downhill from vessel to vessel, from the Crucible to a Gyre (the Vessels, Siphons and Distilling guide). The
Conduit is a fluxionist's bracer, not a cable.

1685.content:
**Distillate is not a fluid**: other mods' pipes and tanks don't carry it. Only the Energistics
branch puts it into an ME network.

1686.content:
**Items** — by the game's slots: hoppers and other mods' pipes put into devices and take from them, as with a chest. On the
Brewing Tower the sides and top take catalysts, the bottom gives the brew; the Molder takes from the storage above it. Current
holders hold no items.

1687.content:
Through-Mirrors carry items far, a Stand-in gives you a block's face from
a distance.

1688.content:
The  turns **the land's flux into energy for other mods' machines**: one flux is 800 units of energy
(FE, one to one across mods). Its store is 8,000; while it isn't full, the mill takes 0.5 flux from the land every half second
and pushes energy to its neighbors on all six sides, at most 400 per step. No consumer — the store stays full, no flux is spent.
The wheel turns while energy goes out.

1689.content: NeoForge — the loader's own energy; Fabric — Team Reborn Energy (machine mods bring it; without it the mill stands).

1690.content: The mod's devices can't **accept** other mods' energy: their energy is the flux of the place.

1691.content:
**A window only where it can't be done without one**: the Flux Workbench, Lens Grinder, Pantograph, Reckoning Desk, Biome
Converter. Other devices take items by a press or a throw (the Crucible catches thrown items), and their state shows on the model.

1692.content:
**The  in hand reads a device instead of opening it**: what the Crucible and a vessel hold, whether a siphon
runs, what's missing. With an empty hand the window opens as usual.

1693.content: **** on your head show what current-holding devices hold when you look at them — hands free.

1694.content:
**A fault shows without a window**: a siphon with "no receiver", a mill with a dry flume, a totem with a dark rune. A window tells
a newcomer why a device stands still instead of "0 of 0".

1695.content: With Jade, the probe shows the distillate, heat, murk and currents of the block under the crosshair.

1696.content:
**A device has no versions.** A tier is another device (the Fluxsteel Retort after the Retort) or an upgrade next to it: Bands
on a vessel, a Gale Fan at the Forge, an Abacus at the Brewing Tower, a Catchment at the Workbench. Each has its own price and
fits only its own device.

1697.content:
**A device of several blocks** is placed as one item (the Gyre, the Brewing Tower — two halves, a broken one drops one item) or
**wakes up from quickdust**: the Flux Forge, the Slipway, the Brewing Tower, the Converter tower. Structures like the Confluence
altar have a plan: the Codex draws it and places a ghost.

1698.content:
**The owner is whoever placed it.** Another player's paired device (mirrors, Ferrystone, Through-Circle, totems) works for you
only if its owner opened it to guests. A server operator counts as the owner.

1699.content: The Crucible — a fluxionist's first device.

1700.content: The Flux Workbench and Artifice Devices — crafting for the land's flux, the Forge, the Molder, the Mill.

1701.content: Current Circles, Totems, Through-Mirrors — workshop devices.

1702.content: Biome Converter — a device that grows a place.

1704.content: The Reckoners' maze: the Wayfinder Cord at a Gauge Stone, the thread back, the Recount of the passages, the Descent Gate, the Summing Lock on the Wheel of currents, traps, the loop's guardians and rewards.

1715.content:
**The Meanders** are where the flux of the world does not run straight but goes round in loops. In its bends the Reckoners built
the **Counting Ways** — a maze of measuring corridors and counting chambers where every current was set against every other. This
is where the order split. You come here for things found nowhere else: one more **Hubstone**, Reckoner Records and the coffers
of their storerooms, the dark stone of the Meanders for building, and the story of why the Reckoners parted into three creeds.

1716.content:
The world is not one big maze but many **loops**. A loop has an end: a maze of 9 × 9 cells, 16 blocks each, on two levels, and you
can walk it to the end. All the Gauge Stones of one land of the ordinary world (1280 × 1280 blocks) lead to one loop; the stones
of the next land lead to another. The Codex entry is ; it opens after Reckoner Records and the
Quickstream.

1717.content:
The way in and out is the , the Reckoners' thread of Ariadne. It is made at the Flux Workbench from
three , a , an opaline and an antimony regulus.

1718.content:
**Descent.** Hold the cord (right button) on the head of a **living**  for three seconds: the cord
winds round the stone, knots light up along the pillar, the stone's flux goes into its head in a funnel of sparks — and you go
down into the loop of this land. Let go of the button, step more than five blocks away or take a hit, and the descent stops with
the knot intact. A fallen stone will not do: it has no head and does not remember its loop.

1719.content: **Knots.** The cord has 12 knots: a descent takes one, an emergency pull two. Mend it with Knotted Cord on an anvil.

1720.content:
**The Thread screen.** While the loop arrives, brass lines draw the maze by themselves on dark parchment, a golden thread with an
opaline bead runs through the passages and ties itself in a knot in the Heart of the loop.

1721.content:
**The thread on the floor.** While the cord is in your hand, golden beads run along the floor from you — the shortest **present**
way to the Tether Hall where you came down. The thread shows the way back, not the way on: the way to the Heart you find yourself.

1722.content:
**The way out is at the Tether**: press the brass post in the middle of the Tether Hall and stay close for two seconds — the cord
winds back and you come out at the foot of the Gauge Stone you tied it to. It costs no knot.

1723.content: **Emergency pull**: crouch and hold the cord for six seconds without moving and without being hit — anywhere in the Meanders.

1724.content:
No one sleeps or sets a spawn point in the Meanders: the walls go on moving while you dream. There is no sky, time stands still,
the passages are dark — bring light.

1725.content:
**The Outer Ways** are the upper level. In the middle is the **Tether Hall**, where you arrive. In one of the quarters is the
**Keyhall**, a round hall with door niches; at the far edge from it is the **Descent**, a well with a spiral stair down. The wing
with the Descent is locked by the **Descent Gate**: seals and a socket for a Knot Key.

1726.content:
**The Heart of the loop** is the lower level. In the middle is the **Summing Hall**, 3 × 3 cells; the **Summing Lock** holds the way
into it, and behind the hall lies the **Vault of the loop**, a cast cell behind seals.

1727.content:
**Rooms** stand in dead ends: counting chambers with tally boards, record rooms with shelves of ledgers, measure storerooms,
cisterns, counters' cells, cave-ins, workshops of unfinished automatons, chapels of the Sum; the rooms hold Reckoner coffers and
journal pages on lecterns (hints for the locks and guardians).

1734.content:
The passages of a loop **move**. Every two and a half minutes the loop recounts: in some doorways a **shoal** grows from the groove
in the floor — amber and lilac of stilled flux — and in others it melts away. Ten seconds before, the **Counting Bell** tolls: the
doorways about to close shimmer amber, the shoals about to melt shed lilac grit. The signs show at every level of "Mod graphics".

1735.content:
**The loop never locks you in.** In either phase of the Recount there is a way to the Tether Hall from every cell: the passages
change, but there is no dead end without a way out. The cord's thread follows the new way from the next second.

1736.content: **A shoal will not rise** on someone standing in the doorway — it waits.

1737.content: Shoals and cast walls do not break: this is a maze. Go round.

1747.content: Beside it on the wall are two to four **Tally Dials**. An empty hand turns a dial to the next rune of a Spring or a Pole (six round).

1765.content: What stagnant flux threatens: the mire threshold, how mire grows and recedes, its blocks and creatures, Roiled beasts, effects, and everything that clears murk.

1778.content:
Flux drawn roughly does not vanish — it stagnates into **murk**: in Crucible remelting, in a broken confluence, in a cheap lens.
Murk does not seep to the neighbors but settles where it was spilled, and it takes the place of flux: a murky chunk refills only up
to "riverbed minus murk". Settled murk above the threshold becomes **mire** — a living blight that creeps over the ground and breeds
creatures. It is hard to stop and very easy to grow.

1779.content:
Entries:  in Basics, then the mire branch of the Stillness chapter: ,

1784.content:
Murk shows by the Loupe's crosshair and without it: murk flakes in the air are dusty lilac, the murkier the surroundings, the
thicker. A **murkcap** in caves is a sign the flux has stagnated there.

1785.content:
Now and then a **seed** settles in a murky chunk — at the lowest spot: murk runs down and gathers in hollows. Even more rarely a
Mire Hummock settles on the mire.

1786.content: Every mire block now and then turns a neighbor — downward and along water sooner than up: mire runs. Only an exposed block turns.

1787.content: **Mire eats murk**: every silted block eats a little of it. Mire crosses into a neighboring chunk only if that one is murky too.

1788.content: Mire does not touch lumenash, murkcaps, Clearwort, the Purifier or the grates.

1795.content:
**Mire Vents** grow on silted soil and trunks: they breathe in four beats, and on the out-breath drive murk into the neighboring
chunk and raise gnats. A **blister** ripens in three stages and bursts with silt or a leech — from a blow or an arrow too.
**Threads** creep across faces and tangle the feet. **Ooze** runs down into hollows and dries; thick ooze in a murky chunk
gathers into a Mire Clot.

1796.content:
Bring the murk below a third of the riverbed, and the mire recedes by itself: Silted Soil to mud, a Mirebound Log to its own log,
crust and blisters to ooze, threads to air, and Silted Stone to . The place's current settles into the
pores of Pitted Stone: a pickaxe without Silk Touch crumbles it to gravel and one time in ten knocks out a shard of the place's
current (Fortune adds 5 % per level). Ooze dries into . A hummock without murk withers on its own.

1797.content: Mire creatures are born only near a player. **Silting** heals them.

Mired; the sediment's name shows above its head.

1815.content:
Set a  on top of the Purifier, or a cluster of them where each touches the next by a face, up to sixteen. Every
5 seconds it takes 0.5 murk for the first grate and a fifth less for each next one (three grates — about 1.2 a turn) and pours as
much flux back. Its fuel is distillate of any current but Murk: a vessel, an Alembic or a Gyre beside it or below, a siphon to its
side or a poured vial; it holds four parts, and one part lasts four turns.

1816.content:
Now and then a grate clogs with silt. Throw a  into running water — in five seconds it
rinses clean.

1817.content: The Loupe on the Purifier tells what it lacks: grates on top, fuel, or that the chunk is already clean.

1818.content: A broken Purifier loses what was poured into it: it goes into its chunk as murk.

1819.content:
A druse grows in three stages, about six minutes each, and each stage drinks 3 murk from the chunk; with less murk it waits. Take it
with a : what it drank stays locked in, and a ripe one gives two druses — one to plant again, one to dissolve
in the Crucible. Broken any other way — by hand, pickaxe, explosion — it bursts, and everything it drank returns to the chunk as murk.

1820.content:
There is a place where murk needs no workshop: in the **Stagnant Backwater** the water has not moved for years and the murk settles
on its own — the land holds a little over a third of its riverbed from birth. Mire lives there through no one's fault, the trees
stand as dead husks, gnats swarm over the water. A cleansed backwater silts up again within hours, and the mire does not spread past
its edge: the neighbors have nothing to feed it. Nobody sets a workshop in a backwater.

1821.content:
A skein with a thread of Murk in it clouds its chunk and makes mire within 8 blocks grow 2.5 times as often, now and then releasing
Murky Glints. It brightens if you clean the chunk while it holds no Murk thread — faster with Halo forced into the skein, or with
a Purifier in its chunk. Details are in the entry .

1822.content: Flux and Murk of the World — where murk comes from and where there is less of it.

1823.content: Dissonance and Visions — the second price of rough work.

1824.content: The Codex of Currents — the Purifier, Clearwort and the Flask are studied at the Desk.

1826.content: Pairs of mirrors and vessels: items go into the pair, the Pocket Mirror sends from your hand, the Ender mirror opens your ender chest, the Deep Mirror steps through the glass, Linked Vessels share one level.

1834.content:
A Through-Mirror is a pair of panes in speculum frames: an item thrown into one comes out of the other wherever it is and goes
into the chest the pair hangs on. Sending costs flux and leaves no murk. Codex entries — ,
 and .

1836.content: Hang the first  on a sturdy face — a wall, a floor or a ceiling.

1837.content:
Press the second mirror against it: one item of the stack remembers it (tooltip "tuned to the mirror at x, y, z", the icon
glows). While it is in your hand a turquoise dotted line runs from the first mirror to where you aim.

1838.content: Place it anywhere — a pair. On a chest or a barrel you hang it sneaking (otherwise they open).

1839.content:
A pair is made only from two lone mirrors. Break one — the other is left alone. The Silvered Glass of the recipe — Flux Workbench:
glass, a speculum sheet, glass.

1840.content:
**In**: an item that touches the glass goes to the pair. A hopper or a pipe above the mirror puts a stack at a time into it.
Pipes can't take from a mirror.

1841.content:
**Out**: what arrives goes into the storage the pair hangs on (a chest, a barrel, a hopper), and what doesn't fit comes out of
the glass. Its mirror doesn't take an item that came out back.

1842.content: **Cost** — flux of the sender's chunk: 0.05 per item, at least 0.25 per send. Not enough — as much goes as is paid for.

1843.content:
**A sleeping pair**: if the pair's land isn't loaded, items wait in its box (up to 9 stacks) and come out when its chunk arrives.
The server doesn't load chunks for items.

1844.content: In the Stillness outside thawed land the glass freezes: nothing goes through, the Loupe says "Frozen".

1845.content:
The owner is whoever placed it. Sneaking with an empty hand, the owner opens the mirror to guests or closes it. Another player's
closed mirror can't be tuned to, looked into with a pocket mirror or stepped through; thrown items and hoppers work for everyone.

1846.content:
— press it against a Through-Mirror (yours or open to guests): it looks into it. In your hand it
sends into that mirror what you hold in your other hand, from anywhere — for the flux of the chunk you stand in: 0.1 per item,
at least one, no more often than every half second.

1847.content:
**The Ender mirror** is the same pocket mirror tuned, sneaking, on an ender chest: in hand it opens your ender chest anywhere
for 0.5 flux, no more often than once a second. Tuning it to a Through-Mirror removes this, and the other way round.

1850.content: the pair is in the same world, neither pane is frozen, there is room to stand in front of the far glass;

1878.content:
Everything a fluxionist starts with lies in the Overworld: opaline and antimony underground, crystal nests in caves, two
current trees and herbs by the water. Beyond that are the mod's own places — forests, mires and caves where the flux of the
world runs its own way and where things grow that grow nowhere else. The Loupe held at open air reads the place — its
riverbed and the currents around; read every new place this way: it is knowledge for the Codex.

1881.content:
**Opaline** is needed by everything that looks into the flux: Loupe glass, Conduit lenses, vessels for distillate. The
**antimony regulus** is the first metal: quickdust is made from it, with copper it casts speculum bronze for instruments, and
it purifies distillate in the Crucible. Without the regulus there is no quickdust and no Codex — keep antimony in stock
(, ).

1882.content:
Where flux has stood still for ages, it crystallizes: in caves from y −56 to 64 grow nests of crystals of the six primal
currents — the four Springs and the two Poles. A pickaxe takes shards from a crystal; shards go into quickdust and Flowstone,
into attuning Gauge Stones, and pay the Flux Workbench for a current the place lacks ().

1892.content:
— the **weeping willow** grows in swamps and on the banks of rivers, lakes and streams, no more
than ten blocks from water. A living willow raises the riverbed of its chunk **1.35 times**: the workshop gets more flux.
One willow in eight is old and **hollow**: in the slit of its swollen butt hide a Reckoner coffer and a Glint Nest; at night
the hollow glows.

1893.content:
— the **lumenash** grows rarely and alone in forests, plains and meadows. Its living leaves turn
the murk of its chunk into flux — **0.02 per second** per trunk, up to three trunks per chunk. A felled lumenash cleanses
nothing: plant it where murk settles.

1894.content:
The **Elder Lumenash** is the oldest lumenash, a trunk of 24–30 blocks with a hollow and a lucent skein inside. That is where
a current skein is found most surely ().

1909.content:
A quiet lowland where the flux of the world stands high: weeping willows lean to the water, lumenashes between them, the ground
is ; Elder Lumenashes rise here more than twice as often as in ordinary forests. **Lumenharts** graze:
every five to ten minutes an adult drops a , and the Flux Forge chars it into
 — without felling a single lumenash. At night **willowkin** step out of the willows: they
leave you alone until you fell a willow or a lumenash at night — then every willowkin within 24 steps comes for you
(). Snagling camps stand in the floodplain too (The Snaglings).

1910.content:
The weald gives **Bloom without brewing**: veins of sap glow on the bark of old sanguine aspens — an empty bottle at such a vein
fills with , and the vein closes and fills again in a few days. Every eight seconds all the veins of the
weald flare at once — that beat is how you know it.  on the trunks is light without a torch and can
be planted on any log. Sanguine slate and the dark wine-red aspen planks make a dark, warm house. The shy **saphorn** roams here:
every few minutes it drops a sprig of living aspen ().

1911.content:
It is always the last hour of autumn here: dark maples with tiers of amber leaves, a leaf falls slowly, and some hang for
a breath. An amber drop swells on the ripe bark of a honey maple — take it with an empty hand: that is ,
**Tempo** straight from the tree. The wound swells again in about half an hour to an hour; only grown maples give resin, not
a log placed by hand. Umberstone is for masonry and sundial tiles, and foxfire glows in fallen maples.

1912.content:
Be careful at night: heaps of leaves lie in the litter, and in some a cream vein smolders — that is a **leafwight**. Closer
than four blocks it rises, and its touch steals Tempo: for three seconds you lag behind ().

1913.content:
Black spires of pine in silver beard lichen and almost black water. The forest gives three things:  —
a wound on an inkpine's bark with a drop of ink, press it (a full refill for the Ruling Pen on a crafting table without
a shard, and generous Gloom for the Crucible);  — the loose sheet of a scrollbark is cut
with shears (paper and Scroll Shelves, which power an enchanting table like bookshelves); and **Reckoner Records** in the
Scriptorium (Ruins). At night **inkblots** rise — their touch sticks and binds — and
hush owls fly without a sound ().

1914.content:
A forest over a seam of Ember has smoldered for ages: black pines with orange cracks, ash, embers rising. The Smolderwood
gives **Ember without going down to lava**: in its Ember seams crystals of Ember grow right at the surface, and in the caves
beneath it every second nest is Ember. You can see an Ember seam from afar at night — a crack in the ground glowing orange;
along its edge lies hot ash that burns like magma: go around or sneak across. In the crack are 
and Ember crystals.

1915.content:
Fallen brands glow and set nothing alight; an axe splits a brand into one or two  — it burns in
a furnace twice as long as coal. Fire does not spread in the Smolderwood. Among the brands lie **brandlings**: they rise on
whoever comes close or chops a brand nearby and bite with fire; water puts them out ().

1916.content:
A delta where rivers braid before the sea and the flux runs thick and wild. Over the channels stand pollard osiers (shears on
an osier's head give , and the head grows back), in the peat lie half-sunken black trunks of
: bog oak has no sapling, its wood comes only from the world. Tall sedge rises above your head,
 glows with warm down,  burns in a furnace. Rods and sedge make the wicker and
thatch set for a hut.

1917.content:
This is the **Snaglings'** home: their bands are twice as common here as in floodplains and jungles, and their stiltholds stand
over the channels. The peaceful **driftback** wanders the shallows with a snag on its back — an empty hand takes the catch off
the snag. All of this is in The Snaglings.

1918.content:
A scar of the Great Stopping: white birches with glass leaves, all leaning one way — in each world its own. The Hourless Wood
gives **Still without the Stillness**: in rain the drops hang here like beads, and an empty bottle raised under open sky
gathers a  — for the Crucible and for the flame of a Lull Lamp. Lullstone and glass leaves make
a dark blue house with amber light. **Glassfinches** hang among the birches, caught mid-flight. The light here is "wrong":
**Laggards** roam by day as well, and morning does not crumble them. Halted caravans stand on old roads
(Ruins; ).

1919.content:
A mire where the water has not moved for years and **murk settles on its own**: the land holds a little over a third of its
riverbed from birth, and mire lives there through no one's fault. Water the color of silt, dead husks of trees, gnats over the
water and gas from the bottom. A cleansed backwater silts up again within hours, but the mire does not spread past its edge
(). Nobody builds a workshop here — you come for silt, murkcaps and business with the Sunken cult: Mire
Shrines and the Sunken Sanctum stand in the backwater (Ruins).

1920.content:
**Silt herons** peck mire leeches and gnats and after three meals drop a lump of silt; approach them sneaking. At night a little
light glows over the water — do not trust it: it is the lure of a **mire angler**, and it snatches whoever comes within six
steps with a lunge from the water. On land the angler is clumsy — draw it onto the bank ().

1921.content:
Caves under gentle land deep inland, where there would otherwise be dripstone caves. An underground vein of flux comes close
to the cave here, and the stone begins to flow. The grottoes are a **mine of currents**: three times more crystal nests, and
any of the six primal currents evenly.  lies as the floor — take it with a pickaxe, no shard needed.
 glow at the bottom of the rimstone pools (for the Crucible and for a Pearl Lamp), and the pools'
**caddises** drop them now and then: a bucket of water carries a caddis to a pond at home. Onyx in the wall layers is a dark
stone for building. A drip hurts whoever falls on it, and one cut from above falls. Deeper stand Reckoners' Wells
(Reckoners in the world; ).

1995.content:
**A second tincture over a guise** meets it on the Wheel: neighbors combine — Gale and Tide give Drift, Strata and Ember Alloy,
Ember and Gale Spark; opposites clash — the guise tears, murk goes into the ground, your eyes ripple.

1996.content: In its home place a guise is half again as strong and lasts twice as long; in a foreign one it is weaker and fades twice as fast.

1997.content:
A guise takes a little flux from the chunk; where flux is below a quarter of the bed, it fades. To drop a guise — the "Shed Guise"
key. After it, no new tincture can be drunk for half a minute.

1998.content:
is a primal shard crushed by weight: put a shard on the ground and drop an anvil, sand, gravel or
a dripstone tip on it — three pinches. Entry — .

1999.content: A pinch of grit in the Atomizer's nozzle keeps its cloud twice as long — for one puff; the nozzle holds sixteen pinches.

2000.content:
**Seasoning**: up to three pinches with food on a crafting table. Whoever eats it gets the effects of the seasoning's currents:
Ember guards against fire, Tide lets you breathe underwater, Gale makes you fall slowly, Strata gives toughness, Lattice a store
of health. Pinches combine on the Wheel, as in the Crucible. To wash seasoning off — a cauldron of water.

2001.content: A drop of distillate seasons too: a vial next to the food on a crafting table gives it one part.

2002.content: The Crucible, heat and clashes: The Crucible.

2003.content: The Brewing Tower and the Atomizer on siphons: Vessels, Siphons and Distilling.

2006.content: The main channel of the flux: the Sluice Arch and its toll in flux, races in the air, isles over a sea of quickwater, a sky of ribbons, biomes, life and places of the Quickstream.

2007.content: The Sluice Arch and the toll

2017.content:
**The Quickstream** is the main channel of the flux. Under the flux of the world runs the main stream: all forty-two currents
flow side by side in it as **races** — rivers of living flux in the air — and the riverbed of every chunk is one of its branches.
You come here for what the world above lacks: by its races the riverbed is twice that of a river, the current of the place is any
of the forty-two, **quickwater** fills the sea under the islands, and the way between two arches through the Quickstream is four
times shorter. The Reckoners measured it with great locks; the Tollkeepers dammed it with barrages and drink it. The Codex entry is
; it waits for your dive into the Lees.

2018.content:
The way in is the same **Sluice Arch** that leads to the Stillness: a 4 × 5 frame of , woken
by a pinch of . But the lock takes its **toll in flux**:

2019.content:
toward the Quickstream the arch wakes if you know the entry "The Quickstream" and the flux of the chunk is **at least
1.4 riverbeds**; once awake, it drinks the flux of the chunk almost to the bottom;

2021.content: you can also raise the flux of the chunk under the arch with quickwater: three or four buckets at once (see "Quickwater" below).

2022.content:
With **three Still Grains** in your inventory the same arch leads to the Stillness: the toll decides the level — stillness leads
to stillness, living flux to living flux (the guide The Stillness).

2023.content:
Awake, the arch fills with the **Quickstream Veil**. Stand in it for 4 seconds: the world speeds up and brightens, ribbons of
currents run in from the edges, and the "Locking through to the Quickstream" screen — lock gates of speculum, the marks of the
chamber and ribbons braiding into the Wheel — lets you out above.

2024.content:
**Coordinates ×4**: your place in the Quickstream is the arch's x and z divided by four; on the way back, multiplied. The passage
builds the arch on the far side itself — on top of the nearest isle within 14 blocks, or on the surface of the sea if there are
no isles nearby.

2025.content:
The arch on the far side leads back. A new arch woken in the Quickstream itself takes no toll and leads home four times farther
from where it stands.

2026.content: Your first arrival is a reading for the Codex; there is no Dissonance: living flux is clear.

2027.content: The isles hang high over a sea of quickwater: a  or a  comes in handy.

2028.content: **You can live here**: beds and spawn points work. The days are half as long, weight is 0.8. There is no weather and no clouds.

2029.content: **The riverbed** by a race is 200, between races 30, deep inside the isles 16.

2030.content:
**Murk cannot settle here**: by a race the stream carries it away. Behind an unbroken barrage the flux stands, and murk gathers
as it does above.

2032.content:
Races are rivers of living flux in the air, **3–9 blocks** across and **6–14 blocks per second**; each has its own current and
color.

2033.content:
**They carry you**: step in and the race carries you along, faster than running. Jump into one even from an isle — it catches you
and holds you. Inside you cannot fall: weight fades away.

2034.content:
**Steer with the keys**: crouch and you go slowly; the movement keys steer across the flow — that is how you step out sideways,
and jumping lifts you toward the edge.

2035.content: Races carry items, creatures and arrows too.

2036.content:
**Confluence**: neighbors on the Wheel merge — races of Tide and Gale flow on below their confluence as one race of Drift. At a
confluence the tributaries' threads braid and swirl into an eddy; you cannot go up a tributary — the stream brings you back.

2037.content:
**Clash**: opposite Springs never merge. Where Tide and Ember, Strata and Gale, Lattice and Fray would meet, there is a rough ball
that throws everything out and gives birth to Clashers.

2038.content:
**Fork**: halfway along, a main race lets out an arm. As you come up to it, press the movement key toward the arm — a short
press is enough — and the arm catches you; press nothing or the other way and the main race carries you on. At a fork the
sideways keys only choose: they never throw you out of the race there.

2039.content:
**The current of the place is the race's current**: within 12 blocks of a race its current is added to the currents of the place.
By a race of Ember the Flux Workbench sees Ember, and Current Seeds grow by a race of their own current — any of the forty-two. The
Loupe, looking into the air at a race, reads its current.

2040.content:
Races rise from the sea of quickwater and fall back into it. In the Braids skeins wind themselves by the races every few minutes
if there are few of them nearby.

2041.content: The sea under the isles is flux in liquid form.

2042.content:
**Fall in and it brings you back up**: quickwater carries a swimmer to the mouth of the nearest race rising from the sea; at the
mouth the water wells up and hands you to the race, and the race lifts you to the isles — step off it sideways. No mouth nearby —
an upwelling column rises by the nearest isle and sets you on its top. Items you dropped are carried onto an isle by the same
column. Crouch to dive — then the water does not carry you. Falling into the sea does not hurt.

2043.content:
**It carries flux with you**: a  poured outside the Quickstream gives the chunk **a quarter of its
riverbed**, but not above one and a half riverbeds, and lies as plain water. This is how the flux is raised under a Sluice Arch or
in a dry workshop.

2044.content: Standing in it slowly heals. It does not multiply: two pools make no new source.

2045.content: **A Crucible** filled with quickwater while empty boils over without murk: the living flux carries the surplus away.

2046.content: **In the Stillness** a poured bucket thaws a circle of three blocks for a minute; it gives no flux there.

2047.content:
There is no sun — the sky is the upper Quickstream itself: across deep turquoise run giant ribbons of currents with wavy veins and
bright heads, and their light is the day. At night the ribbons dim, the turquoise turns blue and stars come out. Toward the horizon —
a pale haze over the sea.

2053.content:
**The Still Brink** is where the Quickstream stops. Time moves in jerks here: in the **pillars of stopped time** (a circle of
7 blocks up the whole height, rime in rings at eye level) everything stops for 10 seconds every 30 — creatures, items and arrows
stand where they were caught, but the player does not: an enemy's arrow hangs in the air, a beast freezes mid-leap. The Stillness
is closest here — bent grass, Still Grains in drifts.

2054.content:
**Racestriders** are the herd beasts of the isles and food for whoever lives in the Quickstream: mutton, leather and, from one you
slay, a pinch of Gale or Tide Grit. A frightened Racestrider leaps into the nearest race, and the race carries it to another isle.
A running person scares them — come at a walk.

2055.content:
**Racefish** are shoals of glassy fish swimming up the races, each with a light in the color of its race. The Loupe reads the
race's current in them — a way to get rare currents.

2056.content:
**Clashers** live in clashes: two halves of opposite Springs strike in turn, and each blow carries the Spring of its half. Hit a
half with a weapon or lens of the opposite Spring and it cracks, its blows weaken; with both halves cracked the Clasher falls apart
and drops shards of both Springs.

2057.content:
**Dustfins** swim in the gray dust of the Drained Isles: only a fin shows above the ground, and whatever circles you is about to
strike from below; the bite leaves you hungry. They cannot swim in stone, tuff or planks — stand on stone.

2058.content:
**Lock Tenders** are Reckoner automatons at the locks and lodges: they set back whatever you turned. Struck, one answers with its
gauge rod and calms down after ten seconds. The Tollkeepers are their enemies.

2059.content: All of them are in the Bestiary.

2060.content:
**The Keeper's Lodge** — a log house on a plinth of Reckoner stone on an isle of the Channel Reaches or the Quick Meadows: a copper
tented roof, a gauge rod with a lantern. The keeper is long gone, his tender walks the porch; inside are a crate, a gauge jar and
a log.

2061.content:
**The Still Outpost** — a broken ring of still masonry on the Still Brink: a tower with an Hour Dial, a brazier with a stopped
flame, two frozen guards and a Sentinel by the tower. The brink caught the watch mid-step; a barrel now and then holds the Rule of
the Still Hour.

2062.content:
**The Toll Barrage** — a Tollkeeper fortress across the main race of the Drained Isles: an old Reckoner lock on a captured isle,
a copper shield in the gap, cisterns of reliquaries on the quays, a camp of Toll Collectors, a Bursar and a Bailiff. Below the gate
the race stands gray and carries no one — that is how a barrage is found: follow the gray race upstream. **Break the barrage** —
and the race flows again, and the Drained Isles around turn green, for everyone and for good.

2063.content:
**The Great Lock** — on the main race of the Channel Reaches: the race runs straight and level through a stone chamber between two
walls. Step into the race upstream — it carries you into the chamber — and step aside onto a quay. Then come two puzzles:

2065.content:
**the lock chamber** behind the door: raise the water with the valves to the lit mark of the pit — and the gate of the vault in
the lower head rises.

2066.content:
The Lock Tenders set back every vane and valve until the puzzle is solved: be quick, lead them away or break them. A pickaxe takes
the masonry of the walls, but the vault is cast on every side — only the gate leads in.

2085.content:
The Reckoners — the ancient order that first measured the currents of the world — left almost everything worth doing in
the world: Gauge Stones that speed up flux, locks and archives with hoards, Records that bring knowledge
(). Their pale gray stone with bronze and measuring scales can be recognized from afar.

2086.content:
A  is the head of a seven-block pillar: a pale column on a stepped plinth, its head girded with
a bronze band and a scale. The stones stand by old riverbeds, on hills, by rivers — in forests, taiga, savannas, plains and
meadows, in deserts.

2087.content:
**Flux twice as fast.** In the 3 × 3 chunks around a stone, flux between chunks flows **twice as fast**: whatever a workshop
has drawn seeps back from the neighbors twice as quickly.

2088.content:
**Channel Record.** The Loupe on the stone's head tells what the stone does to the flux, and each fluxionist's first
reading gives a  — one per stone.

2089.content:
**Cast pillar.** While the head stands, no pickaxe takes the stone and tile of the pillar under it, and nothing — pickaxe,
blast or piston — takes the head itself. Reckoner stone and Marked Tiles are mined in ruins — a fallen stone has no head,
and its pillar is not cast.

2090.content:
There is a socket in the bronze band: set a Spring shard in it (, ,
 or ) and wake the stone with quickdust. An attuned stone **draws flux toward
itself**: at rest its chunk holds about **1.35 of its riverbed**, the neighboring chunks about 1.15, the ring beyond a little
less than the riverbed. No flux is created — the neighbors give it up — but a workshop by an attuned stone in a dry place
lasts noticeably longer. Another shard in the socket breaks the attunement. Poles do not fit the socket: the stone measures
the currents of the Wheel, and Lattice and Fray are directions.

2091.content:
A  is a small stone you build yourself from ruin stone and a Marked Tile at the Flux Workbench.
Flux in its chunk flows **half again as fast** and draws toward the post: the chunk holds about 1.1 of its riverbed. A second
post in the same chunk adds nothing ().

2092.content:
Records are ready knowledge: a Record read with right-click goes straight into the Codex as notes of its chapters, and
entries are studied with those notes ().

2098.content:
A  is the Reckoners' writing in knots: it is not read with right-click but held under the Loupe.
Knotted cords lie in the coffers and barrels of ruins and are sold by the gauger (Villagers).

2099.content:
The Reckoners' hoards are not chests but **coffers** of three grades — ,
 and  — and fragile **gauge jars**.

2100.content:
A **coffer** is opened with an empty hand: the lid lifts, the things jump out, and the coffer stays open and empty.
**Quickdust unseals** a closed coffer — a whirl of Springs, and **one more thing** comes out. A broken closed coffer gives
the same; an open one gives nothing. Coffers hold shards, quickdust, regulus, opaline, Records and cord; sealed ones also
fluxsteel.

2101.content: A **gauge jar** breaks from a blow or an arrow, like a pot, and spills its contents; with Silk Touch it comes off whole.

2102.content:
A **Reckoner Lock** is set into a river bank: a chamber along the river, its lower end in the river itself, and a keeper's
hut — a storeroom behind a gate and a room above ().

2103.content: The storeroom is shut by a : no pickaxe or blast breaks it.

2104.content:
The water is led by  wheels — bronze handwheels on the chamber wall. Each valve has **its own
measure**: one lets in several layers of water, another lets them out. A turn with an empty hand brings the water to "what
was plus the measure"; the excess runs over the chamber's edge.

2105.content:
The gate rises when the water stands **exactly at the lit Marked Tile**. The mark is neither the top nor the bottom of the
chamber, so one valve cannot reach it: you have to alternate the valves.

2106.content: The hint is the keeper's note on the lectern.

2107.content: Spoiler — open the page to read

2108.content: The same valves hold the Flooded Archive — the Reckoners' great dungeon under a riverbed (Ruins).

2109.content:
Now and then six Gauge Stones stand **in a ring around a spring**; next to it lies a broken frame of Reckoner stone, a lucent
skein hangs over the spring, and the banded coffer and barrel hold a Woven Record, cord and a Lattice shard. The ring's stones
**stay silent** until you have revealed the four Springs and the two Poles: "The ring stays silent". The Codex remembers a ring
once read — it is one of the conditions of the Stillness entry, and the broken frame by the spring will matter later
(The Stillness).

2110.content:
Searching for a ring blindly takes long: the  in the Flooded Archive's vault gives everyone
who reads it a map to the nearest ring.

2111.content:
In the Flowstone Grottoes the Reckoners sank wells where the flux comes close to the
stone: a platform of tile on the grotto floor, a well frame with gauge tiles down the shaft (the shaft is full of water, a mark
glows at the bottom), a windlass with a chain and a Pearl Lamp. On the gauger's table are a coffer and a barrel: paper, cord,
a Channel Record, a Tally Tablet, cave pearls, quickdust and shards of the four Springs.

2112.content:
The Reckoners' masons also cut parts of the Confluence altar. The  works as a Plinth, but the
stream of a side Reckoner Plinth to the Heart is **a quarter calmer**. The  works as a Column;
when **all four** Columns of the altar are Reckoner ones, the distillate of every Confluence is **a tenth cheaper** (together
with other discounts — never below two thirds of the price). Both are made at the Flux Workbench from stone and Marked Tiles.

2113.content: The Reckoners help with the Riverbed Task too:

2114.content:
**Cross-Check** — in the deck of any chapter. Played, it spends any Reckoner Record from your inventory, and the
segments of the solution lay themselves down, free, without ink, — up to half its length.

2115.content:
**Read the Marks** — comes when a **Marked Tile** stands within four steps of the Desk: up to four segments of the
solution not yet drawn show through in pencil.

2116.content: Ruins and dungeons — the Flooded Archive, the Scriptorium, Tollkeeper posts and Sunken shrines.

2117.content: Villagers — the gauger and his knotted cord.

2118.content: Events — the stones' Roll Call and the Toll Collection.

2120.content: Stand-in, Ferrystone, Swirl, Canopy and Seeping Masonry

2121.content: Five workshop devices: a block's face where you can't reach it; swapping two 3 × 3 × 3 cubes on a signal; pulling and driving creatures; a one-way floor; a wall that turns to water.

2128.content:
Five devices for the workshop and the home. The **Stand-in** gives you a block's face where you can't reach it; the
**Ferrystone** swaps two 3 × 3 × 3 cubes on a signal; the **Swirl** pulls creatures in or drives them away; the **Canopy** is
a one-way floor; **Seeping Masonry** is a wall that turns to water at a word. Codex entries — ,
, ,  and .

2129.content:
— a carved speculum plinth with an opal eye on every face. **Its faces act as the faces of another block**
up to 8 blocks away: a hopper, a pipe, a Molder put into that block and take from it as if they stood right next to it.

2130.content: Sneaking, press the Stand-in on a block — one item of the stack remembers it (tooltip "remembers the block at x, y, z").

2131.content: Place it: all six faces continue **the same** faces of the target — on a furnace, the top smelts, the side takes fuel, the bottom gives the result.

2132.content:
Sneaking, press a remembering Stand-in on a face of a placed one — that face now leads to the new block (the item isn't spent):
one plinth — up to six neighbors. Empty hand on a face — a line saying where it leads; sneaking — the face is released.

2133.content: The target is in the same world, within 8 blocks, its chunk loaded. No chains: a Stand-in doesn't lead to a Stand-in.

2134.content: **A Stand-in doesn't carry distillate**: currents flow through siphons; tuning to a vessel is refused.

2135.content:
Pipes of other mods see the faces too, fluids and energy as well: a Flux Mill pushing energy into a Stand-in pushes it into the
machine behind it.

2136.content: A thin flux thread sags from a face to its target; with the Loupe or the Diviner's Spectacles it is brighter. Target broken — a loose end hangs.

2137.content:
— a slab of Reckoner sluice stone with a bronze ring, laid in the floor. A pair of slabs, on a signal
pulse at either, **swaps everything in the 3 × 3 × 3 cube above one with the cube above the other**: blocks with their contents
and creatures (the one standing on the slab too). A lift, a secret room, a workshop that rolls out, a store on rotation.

2138.content:
The pair is like a mirror pair: a slab pressed on a lone one remembers it; placed — a pair. One Confluence gives two slabs.
The pair is **within one world only**. The owner opens a slab to guests sneaking with an empty hand.

2139.content: A swap — no more often than every 2 s, when **both lands are loaded** (the server doesn't load them).

2140.content: **Cost** — the flux of each slab's chunk for its cube: 0.1 per block, 0.4 per block with contents. Not enough — refused, nothing touched.

2141.content:
**Don't travel**: the unbreakable (bedrock, barriers), spawners, portals and the End portal frame, respawn anchors, budding
amethyst, the mod's devices with their own links (except the Stand-in and the Swirl), double blocks cut by the cube's edge, and
someone else's place guarded by protection mods. The Loupe tells you what's in the way.

2142.content: With a slab in hand or the Loupe you see a pale dotted cube. In the Stillness outside thawed land the slabs freeze.

2143.content:
— a stone bowl with a bronze ring, flux water whirling inside. **While a signal is on, the Swirl pulls
creatures to the bowl or drives them away.**

2144.content: **Radius** — half the signal strength (up to 7.5 blocks), ±2 blocks in height.

2145.content:
**Whom**: an  with an imprint in the front slot — only that kind. Empty hand on the bowl — by age:
all, adults, babies (to separate calves from the herd). Empty hand on the tablet — take it out. Sneaking — pull or drive.

2146.content: It doesn't touch players, masters and guardians, automatons, creatures on a lead or riding. Villagers — it does: a trading hall.

2147.content: Pays 0.002 flux per creature per second; nothing to pay with — it stops ("Dry" in the Loupe). Without a signal it sleeps.

2148.content: A Totem of the Fold is stronger: a creature it holds can't be driven out of its circle.

2149.content:
— flux cloth stretched in a frame at the top face of a block. **Whoever stands on top is held; from below
and the side you pass through and jump up; crouching, you drop through.** A lid for shafts and wells, a floor over a farm (animals
stand, you go down), steps you jump onto from below. An Updraft stream stops at a Canopy as at a floor.

2150.content:
— Flowstone Bricks with a vein of Tide. Press it with the Conduit or give it a signal pulse — all
connected masonry (up to 64 nearest blocks) "weeps": it becomes still flux water you walk and swim through. Once more — it hardens.
A secret passage without doors.

2151.content: The water doesn't flow and can't be scooped with a bucket. The masonry doesn't conduct redstone.

2152.content: It doesn't harden on the living: whoever is inside is pushed to the nearest free spot; with nowhere to go, that block stays water.

2153.content: Through-Mirrors — pairs and tuning, as with the Ferrystone.

2154.content: Addition devices — the Cradle of Currents and the Imprint Tablet, the tablet's second job.

2155.content: Devices and machines — hoppers, pipes and other mods' energy.

2157.content: What stands in the Overworld: Reckoner ruins, the Scriptorium, the Flooded Archive, Tollkeeper posts, Sunken shrines, homes of fluxionists long gone.

here are not the game's chests but the mod's things: shards, quickdust, opaline, Records for the Codex. Reckoner coffers are
